searchDocs.title: adjustValueByUserPriceLevel​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> adjustValueByUserPriceLevel.adjustValueByUserPriceLevel( player: Player ,-- Player being priced for value: number-- Baseline price to scale ) → number-- Adjusted price Returns value multiplied by the player's price-level factor. The level reported by getPriceLevel (1 to 1000) maps linearly onto a multiplier of 0.001 to 1.0, so the price only ever moves downward from the level-1000 baseline. Yields on the first lookup per player. When the price level is unavailable — a failed or throttled lookup — value is returned unchanged rather than discounted. The result is not rounded; round it yourself before showing or charging it.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> AnimalPenBaseClass.new( propData: PropData, penConfig: PropTypes.AnimalPenConfig-- maxAnimals and maxCapacity ) → AnimalPen Creates an animal pen. Seeds the replica with an empty pen (no eggs, no animals, no drops) atpenConfig.maxCapacity, then hands off to PropBaseClass.new with the CollectItems client allowlist. When restoring from a save on the server, the saved props are first replayed forward through AnimalPenBaseClass:_calculateRetroactiveDrops so the pen reflects what it would have produced while the owner was away. Realm-specific setup afterwards: Server — starts the drop timer and the hatching timer. Client — starts the egg/animal/drop visualization. The owner also gets the collection UI, deferred until building finishes if the pen is still under construction.

searchDocs.title: CollectItems​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> AnimalPenBaseClass:CollectItems( player: Player -- The requesting client ) → () Client-callable entry point for emptying the pen — allow-listed in_allowedClientFunctions, so it is reached via DispatchRemoteEvent. The client calls it both from the collect prompt and automatically when the owner walks inside the pen's radius. Verifies ownership, then clears drops, stamps lastCollectionTime, and fires Collected with the collected table — that signal is what the inventory layer credits from. Every animal's lastDropTime is also reset to now, so collecting restarts the production cycle rather than letting a partially-elapsed interval pay out immediately afterwards. No-ops when the pen is empty, so a spurious call costs nothing.

searchDocs.title: AddDrop​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> AnimalPenBaseClass:AddDrop( itemId: string,-- Item to add one of _origin: CFrame? -- Accepted but unused; drop placement is chosen client-side ) → () Adds one drop of itemId to the pen, respecting capacity, and fires AddedDrop. The public entry point for granting a pen drop from outside the production timer — rewards, admin commands, and so on. Silently no-ops when the pen is already at capacity. UseAnimalPenBaseClass:_addDropBypassCapacity when the drop must not be lost. NOTE Currently unreferenced — the production timer uses the internal_addDropWithData instead. Kept as the supported way for other systems to grant a pen drop.

searchDocs.title: AddProduct​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> AnimalPenBaseClass:AddProduct( player: Player ,-- The requesting client productItemId: string,-- Item id of the egg being placed offset: Vector2 -- Pen-relative X/Z offset in studs ) → () Places an egg into the pen to incubate. Server-only: it is kept off_allowedClientFunctions, since spending the egg is the caller's job. Verifies ownership, that productItemId really is an AnimalEgg, and that the offset is inside the pen. It then enforces maxAnimals against eggs plus animals combined, so a player cannot queue eggs past the pen's eventual animal limit. On success the egg is stored with its placedAt timestamp, the egg type's hatchTime, and a random yaw; the hatching timer takes it from there. Consuming the egg from the player's inventory is the caller's responsibility. Every rejection is a silent no-op: the server path that calls it acts on a client request the UI should already have prevented.

searchDocs.title: getPositionDataFromPivot​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.getPositionDataFromPivot( origin: CFrame ,-- The plot's origin pivot: CFrame -- World pivot of the prop being placed ) → PositionData Converts a world pivot into snapped, plot-relative PositionData — the single funnel every placement goes through. Takes pivot into origin's object space, snaps X and Z to the nearest half stud and the yaw to the nearest ROTATION_STEP, and normalizes a 360° result back to 0 so rotations compare equal.

searchDocs.title: isPositionDataEqual​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.isPositionDataEqual( position1: PositionData, position2: PositionData ) → boolean Whether two placements are the same. Used by PropBaseClass:MoveTo to discard no-op moves. Rotation is compared by absolute value, so -90 and 90 count as equal even though they are visually different. That is deliberate for the intended shapes but means a 180° flip of an asymmetric prop can be treated as no move.

searchDocs.title: validatePositionData​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.validatePositionData(position: PositionData) → boolean Shape-checks a PositionData that arrived from a client: all three fields must be finite numbers and R must be an exact multiple of ROTATION_STEP within one turn either way. This validates the format only — it says nothing about whether the position is inside the plot or free of collisions. Those checks live with the caller.

searchDocs.title: formatModelPoints​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.formatModelPoints( model: Model? ,-- The style model; warns and returns nil if absent style: string-- Style name, used in the assertion messages ) → Points? Extracts the named anchor points from a base style model and returns them asPoints, keyed by part name. Parts nested one folder deep are flattened to <Folder>__<Child> — which is how per-plot points end up as Plot__1, Plot__2 and so on. Every value is the part's bottom surface, so callers can place directly on it. The Points folder is destroyed afterwards: the markers are build-time metadata and must not survive into the live base. Asserts that Spawn, LootCart and a point for every entry in PLOTS exist, so a mis-authored style model fails loudly at load rather than producing a base with unreachable plots. Yields waiting for the Points folder.

searchDocs.title: generatePlot​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.generatePlot( origin: CFrame -- Plot origin ) → ( BasePart ,-- The grid floor {[PositionIndex]: BasePart }-- Per-cell parts; presently empty ) Builds a plot's floor: one invisible GRID_UNITS × GRID_UNITS cell part tagged GRID_FLOOR_TAG, wearing a tiled checker texture that draws the grid rather than instancing a part per cell. The second return value is the per-cell part map. It is currently allocated but never filled — cells are computed arithmetically, so the map exists for a future implementation that needs addressable cell instances (per-cell highlighting, say). Treat it as empty. The caller is responsible for parenting the returned floor.

searchDocs.title: randomizeColorShade​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.randomizeColorShade(color: Color3 ) → Color3  Jitters a colour's saturation and value slightly (hue is left alone — the variance constant for it is 0) so repeated instances of the same asset do not read as identical clones.

searchDocs.title: isHitboxIntersecting​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseUtil.isHitboxIntersecting( hitbox: BasePart ,-- Hitbox being tested origin: CFrame? ,-- Position to test at; defaults to the hitbox's own propIdToIgnore: string?-- Prop id to exclude, e.g. the one being moved ) → boolean Whether a prop hitbox would overlap any other prop hitbox — the collision test that gates placement. Builds an include filter of every PROP_TAG-tagged part in HITBOX_CONTAINER except hitbox itself, then block-casts a temporary part of the same size at origin (defaulting to the hitbox's own CFrame, which is how a stationary prop is re-validated). Include-filtering means terrain, characters and decoration are ignored by construction. propIdToIgnore additionally drops the prop with that id from the results — needed when a prop is being moved, since its own hitbox is still parented in the container at its old position.

searchDocs.title: BaseGameMode​
searchDocs.content: </> interface BaseGameMode { id: string-- Unique round id; stamped on characters as RoundTag players: {Player }-- Players still in the round inactivePlayers: {Player }-- Players who ran out of lives and returned to the lobby playerLives: {[Player ]: number}-- Remaining lives per player playerRewards: State-- UserId to { stat: amount }, the pending payout rewardMultipliers: {[Player ]: number}-- Per-player payout multiplier (placement bonuses) scores: {[Player ]: number}-- Raw score, used for end-of-round ranking playerPassesOwned: {[Player ]: {string}}-- Gameplay gamepass names, scanned at construction stats: {[Player ]: any}-- Free-form per-player scratch space for modes winners: {[UserId]: Player }-- Declared winners; only these are paid teams: {[TeamName]: MinigameTypes.RoundTeam}?-- nil in a free-for-all playing: boolean-- True between Start and Stop time: number-- Seconds remaining in the current countdown countdownText: string?-- Label shown alongside the countdown map: Model? -- The cloned map, parented as GameContainer destroyed: boolean?-- Guards Destroy against running twice isWorldSetUp: boolean-- Whether a map is currently loaded config: MinigameTypes.GameModeConfig-- Mode config merged over the defaults intervalTime: number-- Accumulator driving the once-a-second countdown callback maid: Maid-- Owns every connection made by the round PlayerDied: Signal-- (victim, killer?) — fired on a tagged kill PlayerSpawned: Signal-- (player, teamName?) — fired after a successful spawn Stopping: Signal-- Fired before the stop sequence begins Stopped: Signal-- Fired once the round is no longer playing Destroying: Signal-- Fired as the round tears down } Instance shape of a round. Subclasses may add their own fields freely; stats exists for modes that only need a scratch table and no new type.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode.new( config: MinigameTypes.GameModeConfig,-- The mode's own config props: MinigameTypes.GameModeProps-- Per-round overrides, e.g. a forced map ) → BaseGameMode Constructs a round. Called by a subclass's own .new, which then re-setmetatables the result onto itself. Merges config over MinigameConfig.default, picks the map (props.map if given, otherwise a random entry from config.maps), and calls BaseGameMode:Setup to clone it into the world. The round is not live yet — BaseGameMode:Start does that. It also installs three lifetime handlers, all owned by the round's Maid: PlayerAdded — a player joining mid-round waits for their character, then receives the current countdown, the game music cue and the round-start state, so a late joiner's HUD matches everyone else's. PlayerRemoving — removes the leaver from the round and their team. TEAM_JOIN / TEAM_LEAVE — lets a client switch teams mid-round; joining also spawns the player at their new team's spawn. Gamepass ownership is scanned on a background thread rather than inline, because GamePass.has yields per player and the round must not block on it. The scan only runs if the lobby met the minimum player count.

searchDocs.title: SetLighting​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:SetLighting() → () Applies the mode's config.lighting block to the game's Lighting service — ambient, brightness, clock time and the atmosphere settings. No-ops when the mode declares no lighting. Called on map setup and again in BaseGameMode:Stop to put the lighting back. CAUTION The restore in Stop calls this same method, so it re-applies the mode's lighting rather than the lobby's. A mode that changes lighting leaves it changed until the next mode overwrites it.

searchDocs.title: FindPlayerTeam​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:FindPlayerTeam(player: Player ) → string? Returns the name of the team a player is on, or nil if they are on none or the round has no teams. Searches the authoritative teams lists rather than reading the character's TeamTag attribute, so it stays correct even if the character has been replaced.

searchDocs.title: GetSpawn​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:GetSpawn( team: string?-- Team name to spawn within ) → BasePart  Picks a random spawn point from the map's Spawns folder, or from the Spawns/<team> sub-folder when a team is given. Degrades rather than erroring on a mis-authored map: with no Spawns folder at all it warns and falls back to the map's PrimaryPart (or its first part), so a round still starts with everyone piled on the origin instead of failing.

searchDocs.title: Spawn​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Spawn(data: { players: Player | {Player }, spawns: Folder | BasePart | {BasePart }, loadCharacter: boolean? }) → {Player }-- Players successfully placed Places one or more players at spawn points and returns the ones actually placed — a player who left, died during the call, or whose character could not be built is skipped, so always check the returned list before firing follow-up logic like PlayerSpawned. spawns accepts a single part, a list of parts, or a folder (whose BasePart children are used); each player independently draws a random one. With loadCharacter set, a fresh character model is built and assigned, which is how respawns work; otherwise the existing character is teleported. Players are scattered around their spawn point by a random offset, read from the spawn's SpawnOffset attribute (or a legacy Offset value object), defaulting to ±4 studs — this is what stops a team spawning inside itself. Each spawned character is stamped with the round's attributes: Spawned, the RoundTag round id, and the mode's HealthRegen, UseFallDamage and KeepRagdollInWorld settings. A Died listener is attached that routes into BaseGameMode:HandlePlayerDeath. Aborts and returns an empty list if the round stops mid-call, since character creation yields. Yields when building characters.

searchDocs.title: RemovePlayer​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:RemovePlayer( player: Player , team: string?-- Team to also remove them from ) → () Removes a player from the round (and from team, if given) and rebroadcasts the alive count. This drops them from players but does not clear their winner entry, score or pending rewards — a player who has already won still gets paid if they leave, and their character is not touched.

searchDocs.title: HandlePlayerDeath​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:HandlePlayerDeath( player: Player -- The player who died ) → () Handles a player dying. Wired up automatically by BaseGameMode:Spawn; modes rarely call it directly. First, kill credit: if the character carries a KillTag attribute naming a killer's UserId, that killer is rewarded one kills point and PlayerDied fires with both players. The tag is cleared so a body cannot be credited twice. Then a life is spent. With lives remaining the player waitsconfig.respawnTime, respawns at their team's spawn with a fresh character, and is told their new life count. With none left they are removed from the round, moved to inactivePlayers, and sent PLAYER_INACTIVE — they stay in the world as a spectator rather than being kicked back to the lobby mid-round. Yields for the respawn delay and character creation.

searchDocs.title: EnoughPlayers​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:EnoughPlayers( broadcastMessage: boolean?-- Announce the shortfall to players ) → boolean Whether the round still has the globally required minimum number of players (MinigameConfig.minimumPlayers, not the mode's own config.minimumPlayers). When it fails, it optionally announces the shortfall and — if a map is loaded — stops the round. So this is not a pure predicate: calling it can end the round. Call it after any yield, since players can leave while a mode is waiting.

searchDocs.title: PlayerCheck​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:PlayerCheck() → boolean-- true to continue the round Whether the round should keep going. Consulted every tick ofBaseGameMode:GameCountdown and after every BaseGameMode:AddWinner. Returns false when the round is not playing, when nobody is left, or when every remaining player is already a winner — the last being the "everyone made it, nothing left to play for" exit. Set config.disableWinnerCheck to skip that test entirely, which is what modes need when every participant is expected to win. The all-winners test is a loop rather than a #players == #winners comparison, deliberately: players can die and still be winners, so the two counts drift apart and only a membership scan is correct. If any non-winner is found, the round continues provided the mode's own config.minimumPlayers is still met.

searchDocs.title: GiveWeapon​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:GiveWeapon( players: Player | {Player }, weapon: string,-- Gear id under Shared/Data/Gear mods: {[string]: any}?-- Attributes set on each gear's Tool ) → Tool? -- The last Tool given, so the mode can modify it Gives each player a Gearkit gear (the firebit-dev/gearkit package), equipped, wearing their equipped skin.

searchDocs.title: TeamSetup​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:TeamSetup( teamCfg: {[string]: Color3 }-- Team names to their colours ) → () Creates the round's teams from a { name → Color3 } map, each starting empty. Called automatically by BaseGameMode:Start when config.teams is set; a mode only calls it directly to build teams dynamically. Until this runs self.teams is nil, which is how the rest of the class tells a team round from a free-for-all.

searchDocs.title: TeamPlayerIndex​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:TeamPlayerIndex( player: Player , teamName: string ) → number? Index of a player within a team's roster, or nil if they are not on it. Mostly an internal helper for BaseGameMode:TeamRemove.

searchDocs.title: TeamRemove​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:TeamRemove( player: Player , teamName: string ) → () Removes a player from a team's roster. Asserts that teams have been set up. Only touches the roster — the character's TeamTag attribute and overhead colour are left as they were. Use BaseGameMode:TeamPush to move a player between teams, which keeps both in sync.

searchDocs.title: TeamPush​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:TeamPush( players: Player | {Player }, teamName: string-- Destination team ) → () Adds players to a team, moving them off their current team first if they have one. The supported way to assign or reassign team membership. Keeps the three pieces of team state in step: the roster list, the character'sTeamTag attribute, and the overhead nameplate colour. Players without a character are skipped, since TeamTag has nowhere to live. Asserts that teams exist and that teamName is one of them.

searchDocs.title: TeamAssignPlayers​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:TeamAssignPlayers( playerCallback: (( player: Player , teamName: string, teamColor: Color3 ) → ())?-- Called per assignment ) → () Distributes the round's players across all teams, invoking playerCallback for each assignment so a mode can apply per-team setup as it goes. CAUTION The distribution is i % teamIndex == 0 with teamIndex starting at 1, so the first team matches every player and later teams claim overlapping subsets. Players are consequently assigned more than once, with the last write winning — the in-file TODO acknowledges this. Do not rely on it for balanced teams; assign explicitly with BaseGameMode:TeamPush when balance matters.

searchDocs.title: AddPoint​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:AddPoint( player: Player , diff: number-- Points to add ) → () Adds (or subtracts, with a negative) raw score for a player. Score feeds the end-of-round ranking only — it is not a payout. Use BaseGameMode:Reward for anything the player should actually receive.

searchDocs.title: SetRewardMultiplier​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:SetRewardMultiplier( player: Player , multiplier: number?-- Defaults to 1 ) → () Sets a per-player payout multiplier, applied at Stop to both their rewards and their final score. Intended for placement bonuses — first finisher gets more than second, and so on. Passing nil resets it to 1.

searchDocs.title: Reward​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Reward( player: Player , changes: {[string]: number}-- Stat names to amounts to add ) → () Accumulates rewards for a player: { coins = 10, xp = 5 } and so on. Values add to whatever the player has already earned this round. Any stat that appears in MinigameConfig.pointValues also adds to the player's score, at that stat's configured rate. That coupling is why most modes only ever call Reward and never touch BaseGameMode:AddPoint directly. Rewards are banked, not granted — nothing reaches the player's profile untilStop, and only if they are a winner.

searchDocs.title: GetNumberOfWinners​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:GetNumberOfWinners() → number How many players have been declared winners so far. Useful for placement logic — a mode typically reads this before adding the next winner to work out their rank.

searchDocs.title: AddWinner​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:AddWinner(players: Player | {Player }) → () Declares one or more players winners of the round. Winning is what makes a player eligible for payout at Stop. Each new winner is immediately granted the mode's configured reward.coins and reward.xp. Players already recorded as winners, or who are no longer in the round, are skipped. CAUTION This can end the round. After each winner is added, BaseGameMode:PlayerCheck runs, and if every remaining player is now a winner the round stops immediately. Modes where all participants eventually win must set config.disableWinnerCheck.

searchDocs.title: RemoveWinner​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:RemoveWinner(players: Player | {Player }) → Types.Success-- Whether a winner was removed Revokes winner status, for modes where winning can be lost again. Does not claw back the coins and xp BaseGameMode:AddWinner already banked into the player's rewards; it only removes them from the payout list, so the net effect is that they receive nothing. CAUTION Returns on the first successful removal rather than processing the whole list, so passing multiple players only removes one of them.

searchDocs.title: Announce​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Announce( text: string, timeout: number?-- Seconds before it fades; nil uses the client default ) → () Shows a transient hint banner to everyone in the server, spectators included. Use for round-wide narration ("30 seconds left!"). Compare BaseGameMode:Message, which is a larger, targetable message.

searchDocs.title: Message​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Message( players: boolean | Player | {Player },-- true broadcasts header: string?, body: string? ) → () Shows a header/body screen message. Unlike BaseGameMode:Announce this is targetable: pass true for everyone, or a player or list of players.

searchDocs.title: Countdown​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Countdown( duration: number,-- Seconds text: string?-- Label shown beside the timer ) → () Starts a client-side countdown display for the round's players and remembers the label so a late joiner can be shown the same thing. This is display only — it drives no logic. BaseGameMode:GameCountdown is the one that actually times the round (and calls this for you).

searchDocs.title: DropCoin​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:DropCoin( CFrame: CFrame -- Where to spawn the coin ) → () Drops a physical collectible coin into the map at the given CFrame, with a random spin and a downward nudge. The coin plays an impact sound the first time it touches anything, and awards 4–8 coins to the first player who touches it before destroying itself. It is parented to the map, so it disappears with the map at round end.

searchDocs.title: SetPlayerSpeed​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:SetPlayerSpeed( player: Player , walkSpeed: number?-- Defaults to Util.defaultWalkSpeed ) → () Sets a player's walk speed, or restores the game default when walkSpeed is omitted. No-ops if they have no humanoid. Not reset automatically at round end — the character reload in Stop is what clears it.

searchDocs.title: Loop​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Loop( fn: () → boolean?-- Return truthy to keep looping ) → () Runs fn repeatedly on a new thread until it returns a falsy value or the round stops. Returns immediately — this does not yield the caller, so a mode's Play cannot use it as its only body without also yielding some other way. CAUTION fn must yield at least one frame per iteration. It is called in a tight while loop with no implicit wait, so a non-yielding function hangs the thread. self:Loop(function() task.wait(1) return self:PlayerCheck() end)

searchDocs.title: GameCountdown​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:GameCountdown( duration: number?,-- Seconds; defaults to config.roundTime conditionCheck: ((deltaTime: number) → boolean)?-- Per-second check; return false to end early ) → boolean-- true if the countdown completed with the condition intact Runs the round timer and yields until it finishes. The usual body of a mode's Play. Counts down from duration (defaulting to config.roundTime), starting the client-side display via BaseGameMode:Countdown and stepping self.time every frame. conditionCheck — if given — is called roughly once a second, not every frame, and returning anything but true ends the countdown early. It exits when any of these becomes true: the condition failed, the time ran out, BaseGameMode:PlayerCheck said stop, or the round is no longer playing. The return value distinguishes the first case from the rest. Warns and returns immediately if the round has no config.

searchDocs.title: Start​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Start() → () Runs the round from beginning to end and yields for its entire duration. Called by GameService; modes should not call it. In order: Refresh the player list (people join during voting), and bail out via Stop if the mode's minimum is not met. Per player: drop anyone dead or characterless, assign lives, optionally hide nameplates, stamp the RoundTag, and hide their equipped cosmetic. Dropping players re-checks the minimum as it goes. Build teams from config.teams if present. Call the subclass's Init, wrapped so a throw only warns. Set playing, then auto-spawn if config.autoSpawn — per team into Spawns/<teamName> when teams exist, falling back to the shared Spawns folder if the map has no team spawns. Call the subclass's Play (which yields for the round), or run a default BaseGameMode:GameCountdown if the mode does not define one. Stop, unless the round already stopped itself. Yields for the whole round.

searchDocs.title: Stop​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Stop() → () Ends the round: pays out winners, shows the summary, and cleans up. Safe to call from anywhere, including from inside a mode — BaseGameMode:Start checks whether the round already stopped before calling it again. World teardown runs on its own thread with a 3-second grace period so players see the final moment before the map vanishes; lighting is restored and the map destroyed after it. Then, on the main path: fire Stopping, clear playing, fire Stopped, destroy the Maid (killing every round connection), broadcast ROUND_END and stop the music. Cosmetics are restored for active and inactive players alike, and every character carrying a RoundTag is reloaded. Payout, after a short beat, per winner: Apply config.reward.multiplier × the player's own BaseGameMode:SetRewardMultiplier. Apply the Premium multiplier to xp for Premium members. Apply every gameplay gamepass multiplier the player owns, per stat. Emit an EndWinner with the final rewards and score. Winners are then sorted by score to assign ranks, the whole table is broadcast as GAME_ROUND_SUMMARY (each client also receiving its own local rewards), and coins, xp, points, kills and a win are written to each winner's profile. Finally calls BaseGameMode:Destroy. Yields for several seconds across the teardown.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> BaseGameMode:Destroy() → () Final teardown: fires Destroying and destroys the Maid. Guarded so it only ever runs once, since BaseGameMode:Stop calls it and callers may too. Does not touch the map or the players — BaseGameMode:Stop owns that.

searchDocs.title: Bezier
searchDocs.content: Bezier Third-party bezier curve module for easy creation of bezier curves. Created by bhristt (october 15 2021, updated october 25 2021) and vendored here largely unmodified. A curve is built from control points that may be Vector3s or BaseParts; parts are tracked, so moving one reshapes the curve. Points are managed with AddBezierPoint, ChangeBezierPoint, RemoveBezierPoint, GetPoint and GetAllPoints. Positions and derivatives can be sampled two ways. The ...At methods take the raw curve parameter, which is not evenly spaced along the curve; the ...RelativeToLength methods take a fraction of arc length, which is what you want for constant-speed movement. Arc length is approximated over LengthIterations samples and refreshed by UpdateLength. CreateVector3Tween and CreateCFrameTween drive an instance along the curve, and Destroy releases the part connections. This is vendored code — read the source for per-method detail rather than expecting firebit-style docs on all 14 methods. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. searchDocs.title: Blur
searchDocs.content: Blur This item only works when running on the client. Client Tweens the shared UI background blur. The module returns the tween function directly: local Blur = require(ReplicatedFirst.Util.Blur) Blur(0, 20) -- blur in over the default 1s Blur(20, 0, 0.3) -- and back out, faster One BlurEffect named UIBlur is created under Lighting at require time and reused forever — callers never create their own. Why the Id child Overlapping calls have to cancel cleanly, and Roblox gives no "is this tween still the current one" check. So the effect carries a StringValue named Id. Each call writes a fresh random id into it, and a listener on that value cancels the previous tween whenever the id changes. The call then yields one RunService.Stepped before building its own tween, which is what gives that listener a chance to run. Yields That one-frame wait means this function yields. It is brief, but it is real — do not call it from a context that must return synchronously. from is applied to the blur immediately, before the wait, so the tween always starts from a known size rather than wherever the last cancelled tween happened to stop. Returns the Tween (already playing), or nil if either bound was omitted. NOTE This is the low-level tween. ClientState.activeBlurs is the higher-level bookkeeping of which UI layers currently want a blur; the two are not wired together here. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. All rights reserved. firebit/murder-escape - proprietary and confidential.

searchDocs.title: breakJoints​
searchDocs.content: </> breakJoints.breakJoints( instance: Instance -- Root whose descendant joints are destroyed ) → () Destroys every WeldConstraint, Weld, Motor6D and AnimationConstraint found under instance, leaving its parts free to fall apart. instance itself is not searched for joints — only its descendants.

searchDocs.title: resolveOdds​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.resolveOdds( boxId: string-- key in ShopPricing.BOXES ) → {[string]: number}? Returns a box's own odds table, or [ShopPricing.DEFAULT_BOX_ODDS] when the box omits one.

searchDocs.title: validateBoxes​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.validateBoxes() → () Startup validation, called from [BoxService.init]: for every stocked box in ShopPricing.BOXES, asserts its resolved odds sum to 1 (within SUM_EPSILON) and every rarity with odds > 0 has at least one pool item. error()s loudly on either violation. A box with no pool items at all is unstocked: it warns and is skipped, and BoxService.getBoxInfo reports it as absent so the shop never lists it.

searchDocs.title: getBoxInfo​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.getBoxInfo( boxId: string,-- box to describe player: Player -- player whose pity counter/restriction to read ) → ShopTypes.BoxInfo? Everything the box window needs: price, resolved odds, the box's full pool (sorted rarity then name), the pity guarantee, the buying player's current pity counter, and whether this player is policy-restricted from paid random items (see BoxService.isPlayerRestricted) — the client hides the purchase/open entry point when restricted is true.

searchDocs.title: roll​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.roll( player: Player ,-- roller, for reading/writing pity boxId: string-- box to roll against ) → string?-- rolled itemId, or nil when the box/pool cannot be resolved Rolls a single item for boxId against the player's current pity state, updates and persists the pity counter, and returns the rolled itemId. Inside a protected tier (DuplicateProtection) the item is one the player doesn't own while any is left. Does not grant the item or touch currency — see BoxService.open.

searchDocs.title: open​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.open( player: Player ,-- buyer boxId: string-- box to open ) → ShopTypes.ShopBoxOpenResult? Purchase-and-open in one call — there are no box keys. Order: Flag + boxId validation. PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync — rejects (closed, no debit) when the call fails or reports ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted. Charges the box price in coins, mirroring DailyRotationService.purchase's debit + Sink analytics + refund flow. Rolls (and persists pity) via BoxService.roll. Grants the result via InventoryService.addQuantityToItemId. Below DuplicateProtection.MIN_RARITY grants may repeat by design (trade-ups and quick-sell use them); protected tiers give a new item while one is left. Refunds on any failure past the debit.

searchDocs.title: tradeUp​
searchDocs.content: </> BoxService.tradeUp( player: Player ,-- trader itemIds: {string}-- one entry per slotted copy ) → ShopTypes.ShopTradeUpResult-- { itemId } on success, { error } when refused Consumes TradeUpContract.SLOT_COUNT owned cosmetics of one rarity and grants one random cosmetic of the next rarity that has items ([TradeUpContract.nextRarity] skips empty tiers). The result pool is the next-rarity pool of a box drawn with weights from the inputs' box memberships (an input in N boxes counts 1/N toward each; inputs in no box count toward the whole catalog). When every input shares a subtype and the pool holds that subtype, the pool narrows to it; a protected result tier (DuplicateProtection) then prefers items the player doesn't own. Same policy gate as BoxService.open. The rarity rule and ceiling are [TradeUpContract]'s, the same ones the window slots by. Starter items (InventoryUtil.isStarterItem) are refused. Inputs are only consumed after every check passes; an equipped item cannot be consumed down to zero.

searchDocs.content: </> Character.getDescription( arg: Player | number?-- player or userId whose appearance to load ) → HumanoidDescription  Gets the character description for a player instance or userId. searchDocs.title: Command​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Command { [1]: ( targets: {Player }, ...string ) → ()-- The handler; required ignoreIfDead: boolean?-- Only passes alive players through the targets table noTargets: boolean?-- Doesn't insert targets during command processing minimumLevel: number?-- Minimum user level required to use the command adminsExempt: boolean?-- Admins included in the call are not inserted into the targets table } A registered command: its handler at index 1, plus optional flags controlling how targets are resolved and who may run it. noTargets skips selector parsing entirely, so the caller alone is the target and the first word stays an ordinary argument. adminsExempt is for punitive commands — it drops superusers from the target list so they cannot be hit by all.

Returns nil when the text does not start with the / prefix. searchDocs.content: On this page CollectionObject Show Private CollectionObject is a wrapper for CollectionService instances found using CollectionWatcher. searchDocs.content: </> Confetti.ui( parent: GuiObject ,-- Where the pieces live (must not clip descendants) origin: Vector2? -- Absolute screen position of the burst ) → () → ()-- Cancels the burst Bursts confetti inside a GUI. Pieces are plain Frames parented to a full-size container under parent, thrown in an upward fan from origin (absolute screen pixels; defaults to the centre of parent, resolved in scale so it holds before layout) and pulled down by gravity until they fade out. Plays the pop sound. searchDocs.content: </> Confetti.portal( source: GuiObject ,-- What the burst belongs to; its centre is the default origin origin: Vector2? -- Absolute screen position of the burst ) → () Confetti.ui on a ScreenGui of its own, one DisplayOrder above the one holding source. Nothing in source's tree owns the burst, so a clipping ancestor (a ScrollingFrame) can't cut it and closing the window, switching its tab or unmounting source mid-burst leaves the pieces flying. The layer copies the source ScreenGui's inset settings, so origin (absolute pixels as source reports them) lands on the same spot, and it is destroyed after the burst. A source outside any ScreenGui (a UI Labs story) bursts in place through Confetti.ui instead.

searchDocs.content: </> interface Result { part: BasePart -- Part found inside the cone angle: number-- Degrees between the ray and the part, within the cone } One hit. Sort on angle to get the part nearest the cone's axis.

searchDocs.title: ConeCast​
searchDocs.content: </> ConeCast.ConeCast( ray: Ray ,-- Origin and direction of the cone's axis angle: number,-- Half-angle of the cone in degrees depth: number?,-- Cone length (defaults to the ray's direction magnitude) overlapParams: OverlapParams?-- Filter passed to the underlying bounds query ) → {Result} Casts in a cone shape from the origin of the ray towards its direction, returning every part whose centre falls within angle degrees of the axis. angle is the half-angle from the axis, in degrees, so 45 describes a 90-degree cone. If no depth is provided, the ray's direction magnitude is used. Results are unordered and unfiltered by line of sight — a part behind a wall is still reported. Use overlapParams to exclude the caster's own character, and follow up with a raycast if occlusion matters. local hits = ConeCast(Ray.new(muzzle.Position, muzzle.CFrame.LookVector * 60), 20) for _, hit in hits do applyDamage(hit.part, 1 - hit.angle / 20) end

searchDocs.title: ControlsData
searchDocs.content: ControlsData Single source of truth for every gamepad bind in the game (and the keyboard keys that mirror gamepad-first actions). Feature code requires this instead of inlining Enum.KeyCode.Button* literals so the whole controller layout is auditable in one place — and so a new bind can be checked against the budget below before it ships. Keyboard-first keys that predate this file (reload R, drop G, quick-buy Z/X/C + B/N/M, arena packs H/J/K, tier T, hotbar 1-0) stay declared in their feature files; only their gamepad twins live here. Gamepad button budget (keep in sync when editing): A: vehicle exit / GUI activate (engine); game-over continue (bound only while the run-end takeover is on screen); round summary Continue (bound only while the summary is on screen) B: modal close, RV repair (guarded), arena pack 3 (L1 chord), queue leave (B = "back out" — modals sink B first, so an open modal closes before a second press leaves the queue) X: reload, queue vote-skip, arena pack 1 (L1 chord) Y: drop weapon, queue mode toggle (lobby picker), arena pack 2 (L1 chord) L1: chord modifier (quick-buy upgrades, arena packs, inventory) L2: melee, trap rotate (priority-gated pair) L3: sprint R1: hotbar cycle (bare), settings toggle (L1 chord, console only) R2: shoot, consumable use, trap place, vehicle gas (context-gated) R3: arena auto-skip toggle (level) DPad L/U/R: quick-buy slots (bare = traps, L1 = upgrades); queue party size 1/2/3 while the lobby picker shows DPad Down: buy weapon tier; inventory toggle (L1 chord); queue party size 4 while the lobby picker shows; focus the lobby side menu (bare, main place, not queued — disjoint from every other DPadDown role) DPad Up also = PLAY (join best queue) in the lobby while NOT queued — disjoint from its size-2 role, which only exists while queued Thumbstick2: camera look / auto-aim break / skill tree preview

The tween is not started — call :Play() yourself. local tween, value = CreateTween(0, 100, TweenInfo.new(2)) value:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Value"):Connect(function() bar.Size = UDim2.fromScale(value.Value / 100, 1) end) tween:Play()

searchDocs.title: CrownGrab​
searchDocs.content: </> interface CrownGrab { maid: Maid-- Owns this mode's own connections, separate from the round Maid crownHolders: {[Player ]: boolean}-- Who is currently crowned touched: {[string]: boolean}-- Unused } Round state, on top of everything inherited from BaseGameMode. CAUTION maid shadows the round Maid that BaseGameMode allocates, since the constructor assigns to the same field after the base has already set it. The base class's own connections are consequently owned by a Maid nothing holds a reference to, and are never cleaned up.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> CrownGrab.new(props: MinigameTypes.GameModeProps) → CrownGrab Creates a Crown Grab round and immediately crowns every other player in the round list, so the field starts split between holders and hunters. Also watches for leavers so a departed player does not keep a phantom crown incrownHolders and hold the round open. Handout happens here rather than in an Init hook, which means it runs before BaseGameMode:Start has spawned anyone — players without a living character at construction time are silently skipped by CrownGrab:GiveCrown.

searchDocs.title: GiveCrown​
searchDocs.content: </> CrownGrab:GiveCrown( player: Player -- Who to crown ) → () Crowns a player: attaches the crown accessory, slows them toHOLDER_WALK_SPEED, and records them in crownHolders. Refuses when the player is dead, has no character, or is already wearing a crown — the last check is what keeps a hunter from accumulating crowns. The steal handler on the crown's handle is armed 0.4s later, so the player you just took it from cannot instantly take it back. When it fires, the old wearer is un-crowned and their speed restored, the crown instance is destroyed, and this method recurses to crown the thief with a fresh one. A death listener removes the crown from crownHolders if the wearer dies, which permanently removes that crown from the round.

searchDocs.title: Play​
searchDocs.content: </> CrownGrab:Play() → () The round. Called by BaseGameMode:Start and yields until the countdown ends. After a two-second grace period it runs BaseGameMode:GameCountdown with a per-second condition that keeps the round alive only while at least one crown exists — so a round where every holder dies ends immediately rather than running out the clock with nothing to contest. Whoever is still crowned when it ends is declared a winner. Multiple winners are normal.

searchDocs.title: Stop​
searchDocs.content: </> CrownGrab:Stop() → () Cleans up this mode's own connections. DANGER This overrides BaseGameMode:Stop without calling it. None of the base teardown runs: winners are never paid, the round summary is never broadcast, playing is never cleared, the map is never destroyed and characters are never reloaded. Since BaseGameMode:Start finishes by calling self:Stop(), a Crown Grab round ends by cleaning one Maid and leaving everything else live. Stop is not part of the subclass contract described on BaseGameMode; mode-specific teardown belongs on the Stopping or Destroying signals instead.

searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.init() → () Registers the coins developer-product receipt callback with MarketplaceData. searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.set( player: Player ,-- balance owner currencyType: string,-- key under stats amount: number-- new balance, must be >= 0 ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the write applied number?-- the new balance ) Overwrites a balance outright. Rejects negative amounts. Prefer CurrencyService.add / CurrencyService.take for gameplay flows — set discards whatever the balance was, so two concurrent grants can clobber each other. Note that setting a balance to exactly 0 returns false: the success check treats the resulting 0 as absent.

searchDocs.title: add​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.add( player: Player ,-- balance owner currencyType: string,-- key under stats amount: number-- amount to credit, must be > 0 ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the write applied number?-- the resulting balance ) Credits a balance. The amount is floored, and must be strictly positive — use CurrencyService.take to remove currency rather than adding a negative. Reads the current balance inside the mutator, so it is safe against the balance having moved since the caller last read it. local ok, newBalance = CurrencyService.add(player, "coins", 250)

searchDocs.title: take​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.take( player: Player ,-- balance owner currencyType: string,-- key under stats amount: number,-- amount to debit, must be > 0 override: boolean?-- allow the balance to go negative ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the debit applied number?-- resulting balance on success, current balance on insufficient funds ) Safe debit that will not allow the currency to go below 0 unless overridden. The amount is floored and must be strictly positive. The balance is checked before the mutation: when the player cannot afford it and override is not set, nothing is written and the call returns false alongside the player's current balance so the caller can report the shortfall. Passing override skips the affordability check and permits a negative balance. local ok, balance = CurrencyService.take(player, "coins", price) if not ok then -- `balance` is what they actually have end

searchDocs.title: setMultiple​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.setMultiple( player: Player ,-- balance owner updates: {[string]: number}-- currencyType -> new balance ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the write applied {[string]: number}?-- the updates table passed in ) Overwrites several balances in a single replicated mutation. Every amount must be >= 0 or the whole call is rejected before anything is written. Returns the request, not the result Unlike CurrencyService.set, the second return value is the updates table you passed in, not the resulting balances — for a set these coincide. Note also that the math.floor in the validation loop assigns to the loop variable and is discarded, so unlike the singular variants these amounts are stored unfloored.

searchDocs.title: addMultiple​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.addMultiple( player: Player ,-- balance owner updates: {[string]: number}-- currencyType -> amount to credit ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the write applied {[string]: number}?-- the updates table passed in ) Credits several balances in a single replicated mutation. Every amount must be > 0 or the whole call is rejected before anything is written. Returns the deltas, not the balances The second return value is the updates table you passed in — the amounts added, not the resulting balances. Read them back with CurrencyService.fetchStats if you need the totals. The math.floor in the validation loop is discarded, so amounts are stored unfloored.

searchDocs.title: takeMultiple​
searchDocs.content: </> CurrencyService.takeMultiple( player: Player ,-- balance owner updates: {[string]: number},-- currencyType -> amount to debit override: boolean?-- allow balances to go negative ) → ( boolean?,-- whether the debit applied {[string]: number}?-- the updates table passed in ) Debits several balances in a single replicated mutation. Every amount must be > 0, and — unless override is set — every balance is checked for affordability before any of them are debited, so the batch is all-or-nothing: a player short on any one currency has none of them taken. Returns the deltas, not the balances As with CurrencyService.addMultiple, the second return value is the updates table you passed in, and the validation loop's math.floor is discarded.

searchDocs.title: DefaultProps
searchDocs.content: DefaultProps This was created because React currently does not have a way to set default properties for components. DefaultProps is a higher-order function that takes a table of default properties and returns a function that takes a table of properties. The returned function will merge the default properties with the provided properties and return the result. local DefaultProps = require(src.Util.DefaultProps) local defaultProps = { foo = "bar", } local createProps = DefaultProps(defaultProps) local MyReactComponent = function(props) props = createProps(props) print(props.foo) -- "bar" end MyReactComponent() Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. searchDocs.title: DataController
searchDocs.content: DataController This item only works when running on the client. Client Bridges the server's Profile Replica into ClientState and gates the client boot on it. :::danger The whole client boot blocks hereEntry.client.luau step 3 waits on this controller before it will bootstrap any other controller, tear down the loading screen, dispatch READY, or mount the React app: local DataController = require("./Features/Core/Controllers/DataController") if not DataController.didLoad then DataController.Loaded:Wait() end Nothing downstream ever has to defend against empty player data — but by the same token, if the Profile Replica never arrives the client stops at a loading screen. There is no timeout here. ::: What it does At require time it connects to Replica.Client.getReplicaAddedSignal("Profile", true). The true fetches any replica that already exists, so requiring this module late still resolves. On the first (and only the first — later replicas are ignored) Profile replica: DataController.replica is set. The replica's whole data table is pushed into ClientState.playerData. didLoad flips true and Loaded fires once, releasing the boot gate. A GetKeyChangedSignal connection is opened for every top-level key in DataTemplate(LocalPlayer), each writing back into ClientState.playerData through SetPath. Keys absent from the template are not mirrored. From there the flow is one-way: server writes the profile, the replica replicates it, this controller mirrors it into ClientState, and components read ClientState. Nothing here writes to the server — profile mutations go out as red actions. StatsController sits one layer further down, mirroring playerData.stats into the scalar ClientState.coins / ClientState.xp states. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. All rights reserved. firebit/murder-escape - proprietary and confidential.

searchDocs.title: hasTouchControls​
searchDocs.content: </> Device.hasTouchControls() → boolean Whether on-screen touch controls are in play — touch is enabled and this is not a console. Distinct from [Device.isMobile]: a laptop with a touchscreen answers true here and false there.

searchDocs.title: getBreakpoint​
searchDocs.content: </> Device.getBreakpoint() → Breakpoint  The breakpoint matching the current screen width. Walks the thresholds largest-first and returns the first one the width exceeds, so a width below every threshold lands on the smallest. Note that several breakpoint names share a pixel value (phone-small and phone are both 640, and everything from laptop-medium up is 1536), so the name returned for a shared value is whichever the flipped lookup table happens to hold — compare with Device.inBreakpoint rather than testing this for equality.

searchDocs.title: inBreakpoint​
searchDocs.content: </> Device.inBreakpoint( target: Breakpoint -- Upper bound to test against ) → boolean Whether the current breakpoint is at or below target — the "max-width" test, so inBreakpoint("phone-large") is true on every phone and false on tablets and up. This is the intended way to branch on screen size; it compares pixel thresholds rather than breakpoint names, so aliased names behave sensibly. Reads the cached lastBreakpoint rather than re-measuring.

searchDocs.title: DodgeTheTeapots​
searchDocs.content: </> type DodgeTheTeapots = BaseGameMode Adds no state of its own; it is a BaseGameMode. Per-round bookkeeping (the difficulty ramp and the set of players currently ineligible to re-score) lives as locals inside Play.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> DodgeTheTeapots.new(props: MinigameTypes.GameModeProps) → DodgeTheTeapots Creates a Dodge the Teapots round.

searchDocs.title: Play​
searchDocs.content: </> DodgeTheTeapots:Play() → () The round. Called by BaseGameMode:Start and yields until the countdown ends. Wires the Finish part: the first time a player touches it they are declared a winner, given a placement-based reward multiplier, congratulated with confetti, and returned to the spawn. Difficulty rises by 0.2 per finish. A local winners set gates re-scoring — it is cleared 1.8s after the teleport, so a player can run the course again, but only their first finish set their multiplier. In parallel a BaseGameMode:Loop spawns teapots in bursts of ten, waiting i / 6 / difficulty * 10 between each — so throws within a burst get further apart while rising difficulty pulls the whole burst tighter. The loop returns false as soon as the round stops. Finally yields on BaseGameMode:GameCountdown for the configured round time.

searchDocs.title: DropData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface DropData { origin: Vector3? -- Spawn point. Defaults to the character's PrimaryPart position originSpread: boolean?-- Randomize the spawn point tweenTarget: Vector3? -- Landing point before the ground raycast. Defaults to origin targetSpread: boolean?-- Randomize the landing point. Forced true when tweenTarget is nil particle: BasePart | string-- Part to clone, or an image asset id rendered as a billboard lifetime: number?-- Seconds before expiry. Defaults to DROP_LIFETIME onClaim: (() → ())?-- Fired on claim, and on cleanup when the drop was never claimed tweenToCharacterOnClaim: boolean?-- Fly to the character on claim instead of vanishing destroyOnArrival: boolean?-- Skip the idle float; retire as soon as the arc lands autoClaimOnDestruction: boolean?-- On expiry, force a pickup instead of a silent removal } Everything a caller can ask for when spawning a drop. Only particle is required. If tweenTarget is omitted, the origin doubles as the target and targetSpread is forced on, so a drop always travels somewhere rather than landing on itself. Both spread flags apply a random offset of up to DROP_SPREAD_RADIUS studs horizontally and 0..2 vertically.

searchDocs.title: Drop​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Drop { particle: BasePart -- The live instance in Workspace targetPosition: Vector3 -- Ground position the arc lands on; claim distance is measured to this lifetime: number-- Resolved seconds before expiry createdAt: number-- os.clock() at spawn onClaim: (() → ())?-- Caller's claim callback tweenToCharacterOnClaim: boolean?-- Fly to the character on claim autoClaimOnDestruction: boolean?-- Force a pickup on expiry claimed: boolean?-- Set once claimed; freezes all position updates tweenInProgress: boolean?-- A pickup lerp is running destroyOnArrival: boolean?-- Retire on landing instead of floating } The resolved form of a DropData, returned by DropsController.spawnDrop. claimed and tweenInProgress are the two guards that keep the animation systems from fighting: once claimed is set, the idle float disconnects itself and nothing else may move the part.

searchDocs.title: getPlayerRootPosition​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.getPlayerRootPosition() → Vector3?  Position of the local character's PrimaryPart, or nil when there is no character. Used as the default spawn origin.

searchDocs.title: spawnDrop​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.spawnDrop( data: DropData-- Drop description ) → Drop? Spawns one drop and starts its arc. Returns the resolved Drop, or nil if no origin could be determined (no data.origin and no character). data.particle accepts either an Instance to clone or an image asset id; a string builds an invisible part carrying a 24x24 BillboardGui with that image, so UI-style drops and 3D-model drops share one code path. DropsController.spawnDrop({ particle = ReplicatedStorage.Assets.Resources.Stone:Clone(), origin = hitPosition + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0), tweenToCharacterOnClaim = true, autoClaimOnDestruction = true, onClaim = function() DropsController.showChange(1, "item", "Stone") end, }) CAUTION When data.onClaim is set the particle is not added to the maid directly — the maid's cleanup function fires onClaim and then destroys the part, unless a pickup lerp still owns it. That is why claimed parts are tracked separately in claimedParts.

searchDocs.title: updateDrops​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.updateDrops() → () Expiry sweep. Driven every RenderStepped by the connectionDropsController.init opens; safe to call by hand. Retires every drop older than its lifetime, skipping any already destroying. Drops flagged autoClaimOnDestruction go through DropsController.pickupDrop with forcePickup so their onClaim still runs; the rest are dropped with DropsController.removeDrop.

searchDocs.title: removeDrop​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.removeDrop( dropId: string-- Key into the active-drops table ) → () Retires one drop without claiming it: marks it destroying, destroys the particle (with a CoinDespawn burst when SHOW_DESPAWN_VFX is on), destroys the maid, and clears it from activeDrops and claimedParts. Note the maid's own cleanup still fires onClaim if the drop had one — so a caller relying on onClaim for the reward is not silently skipped when the drop is removed rather than picked up. Unknown ids are ignored.

searchDocs.title: clearAllDrops​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.clearAllDrops() → () Destroys every active drop's maid and resets the registry and the id counter. Used by DropsController.shutdown and by anything that needs a clean slate, such as a teleport or round transition. Unlike DropsController.removeDrop this does not destroy particles directly — it relies on each maid's cleanup, which means onClaim callbacks still fire.

searchDocs.title: showChange​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.showChange( amount: number,-- Added to the running total for this unit unitType: "coins" | "item",-- Which family of gain itemId: string?-- Item to resolve an icon for, when unitType is "item" ) → () Floating "+N" popup welded to the local character. Independent of the drop system — call it whenever a currency or item total moves. Calls coalesce. The first call clones Assets.UI.GainVFX, welds it to the PrimaryPart and tweens its StudsOffset upward over PARTICLE_TEXT_LIFE seconds. Subsequent calls within that window add to the running total and push the expiry out instead of spawning a second billboard, so a burst of ten single-coin awards reads as one "+10". Each distinct {unitType}_{itemId} gets its own label row cloned from the billboard's Template, so mixed gains stack: DropsController.showChange(1, "coins") DropsController.showChange(1, "item", itemId) Icons resolve from Items[itemId].icon for items and CoreImages["styled/coin"] for coins; a row with no icon falls back to showing the identifier as text and destroys its icon label. No-ops when the character has no PrimaryPart.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.init() → () Bootstrap hook. Resets the registry and opens the RenderStepped connection that drives DropsController.updateDrops. Paired with DropsController.start, which opens the claim loop. Both are called by Bootstrap during Entry.client.luau step 4.

searchDocs.title: pickupDrop​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.pickupDrop( dropId: string,-- Key into the active-drops table forcePickup: boolean?-- Bypass the radius, delay and arrival checks ) → () Claims one drop, if it is claimable. Called for every active drop each frame by DropsController.checkClaims, and directly with forcePickup = true by DropsController.updateDrops for drops flagged autoClaimOnDestruction. Unless forcePickup is set, the drop is skipped when any of these hold: it is flagged destroyOnArrival (it was already retired on landing) the character is further than DEFAULT_CLAIM_RADIUS studs from targetPosition less than CLAIM_DELAY seconds have passed since spawn it is already claimed, or currently destroying With tweenToCharacterOnClaim, the spawn maid is destroyed outright to stop the float, the trail is re-enabled, and a fresh RenderStepped connection lerps the part toward the character's pivot — re-read every frame — over CHARACTER_TWEEN_TIME, after which the part is destroyed and the entry cleared. Otherwise onClaim is spawned and the drop goes straight to DropsController.removeDrop. Both paths play item-pickup. CAUTION Errors on an unknown dropId — it indexes activeDrops without a guard.

searchDocs.title: checkClaims​
searchDocs.content: </> DropsController.checkClaims() → () Claim sweep. Driven every RenderStepped by the connectionDropsController.start opens. Bails early when there is no character pivot, otherwise offers every active drop to DropsController.pickupDrop, which applies the radius and delay checks per drop.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> GameService.init() → () Bootstrap hook. Sets up the lobby loop and the client-facing game mode data. Game mode modules are cloned into ReplicatedStorage so clients can read the configs (names, descriptions, round times) needed to render vote cards — but each clone's Init child is destroyed first, so the server-only round logic is never replicated. It then installs the Heartbeat lobby loop described on GameService, plus a handler that catches up newly loaded players: anyone joining during an intermission receives the remaining countdown and the right music cue, and anyone joining an under-populated lobby is told how many more players are needed. The "need N more players" hint is rate-limited to one everyINSUFFICIENT_HINT_INTERVAL seconds, except that a change in N sends immediately — so the count visibly ticks down as people join rather than lagging behind. No-ops entirely when the Minigames feature flag is off.

searchDocs.title: voteWrap​
searchDocs.content: </> GameService.voteWrap() → MinigameTypes.VotePoolItem?-- The chosen mode and map Runs the map/mode vote and yields until it resolves, returning the winning candidate or nil if no vote could be held. DANGER Returns DEBUG_GAME immediately if that constant is set — which it currently is. Everything below this line is dead until it is cleared. See GameService. Builds a pool by filtering the registered modes down to those whoseminimumPlayers the lobby can satisfy, then drawing up to MinigameConfig.voteSlots of them at random, each paired with a random map from its own map list. Returns nil if nothing qualifies, and short-circuits without a vote if exactly one candidate survives. With a real pool it starts VoteService, broadcasts the vote countdown, and waits on either VoteEnded or a votingTime timeout — whichever comes first, with the loser cancelled. Players who load mid-vote are folded in and given the remaining time rather than a fresh timer, and are skipped entirely once fewer than two seconds remain. Afterwards it prunes voters who left, asks VoteService for the winner, shows the result to the surviving voters, and returns the winning candidate.

searchDocs.title: gameWrap​
searchDocs.content: </> GameService.gameWrap() → () Runs one complete round and yields for its entire duration. Called by the lobby loop; it sets inProgress on entry, and the caller clears it on return. Chooses the round in priority order: a game a player paid to queue viaMinigameService.getNextQueuedGame wins outright, otherwise GameService.voteWrap decides. It then constructs the mode — which loads the map as a side effect ofBaseGameMode.new — records it as activeGameMode, and clears that reference when the round destroys itself. Before starting it waits out an estimated map load time scaled by part count (see MinigameUtil.calculateMapLoadTime), then broadcasts the round info card (mode, map, description, thumbnail, length, lives, teams) and waits four seconds for players to read it. Player count is re-verified before every one of those waits and again after, because each yields; a lobby that drains below the mode's minimum tears the round down and returns rather than starting an unplayable game. Finally calls BaseGameMode:Start, which yields until the round is over.

searchDocs.title: subtractQuantityFromItemId​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.subtractQuantityFromItemId( player: Player ,-- inventory owner itemId: string,-- item to consume quantityToSubtract: number,-- how much to remove recordId: string?-- restrict consumption to this record only ) → boolean-- false when the full quantity could not be removed Removes a quantity of an item across however many records hold it, draining oldest records first (records are sorted by createdAt ascending). searchDocs.title: addQuantityToItemId​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.addQuantityToItemId( player: Player ,-- inventory owner itemId: string,-- item to add quantityToAdd: number,-- how much to add; must be positive props: {[string]: any}?-- per-record props; forces a dedicated record ) → ( boolean,-- false on bad arguments or a missing profile {Types.ItemRecord}?-- the records newly created (not the topped-up one) ) Adds a quantity of an item, stacking into existing records and spilling into new ones as needed. Without props: tops up the first record for that item that is below InventoryData.MAX_STACK, then mints additional full-or-partial records until the requested quantity is placed. With props: skips stacking and always creates exactly one new record, because prop-bearing records are not interchangeable with plain ones. Each new record is placed in the first free hotbar slot (InventoryService.getFirstAvailableSlot); if the hotbar is full it gets a bagIndex from InventoryService.getNextBagIndex instead. Every new record is dispatched to the client as ITEM_SHOP_ITEM_ADD.

Works by sorting the inventory array by slotIndex ascending — bag records sort last because their nil index is treated as math.huge — so the hotbar records land in array positions 1 .. n and each is then assigned its own array position as its new slotIndex. Bag records are skipped and keep their bagIndex untouched.

searchDocs.title: cleanBagIndexes​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.cleanBagIndexes( player: Player -- inventory owner ) → boolean-- false only when no profile is loaded Cleans up bag indexes to be sequential starting from 1 — closes any gaps. The mirror of InventoryService.cleanSlotIndexes, sorting on bagIndex instead so bag records occupy array positions 1 .. n and take those positions as their new indexes. Hotbar records sort last and are skipped. This is the only thing that reclaims the gaps left byInventoryService.getNextBagIndex's monotonic allocation, so it should run after any batch of bag removals.

searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.setItemSlot( player: Player ,-- inventory owner recordId: Types.RecordId,-- record to place slotIndex: number?-- target hotbar slot, or nil to clear ) → boolean-- false when the slot is taken or the record is missing Assigns a record to a hotbar slot, refusing the write when that slot is already occupied. Passing slotIndex = nil clears the record's slot and skips the occupancy check. Does not touch bagIndex — callers moving an item into the hotbar must also call InventoryService.unsetItemBagIndex to preserve the one-index-only invariant.

searchDocs.title: unsetItemSlot​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.unsetItemSlot( player: Player ,-- inventory owner recordId: Types.RecordId-- record to clear ) → boolean Clears a record's hotbar slot, freeing it for another item. Shorthand forInventoryService.setItemSlot with a nil slot. Leaves the record with neither index set, so the caller is expected to follow up with InventoryService.setItemBagIndex.

searchDocs.title: setItemBagIndex​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.setItemBagIndex( player: Player ,-- inventory owner recordId: Types.RecordId,-- record to reindex bagIndex: number?-- new bag index, or nil to clear ) → boolean-- false when the record is missing Assigns a record's bag index. Passing nil clears it. No collision check Unlike InventoryService.setItemSlot, this performs no uniqueness check — two records can end up sharing a bagIndex if a caller supplies a literal value. Always source the index from InventoryService.getNextBagIndex.

searchDocs.title: unsetItemBagIndex​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.unsetItemBagIndex( player: Player ,-- inventory owner recordId: Types.RecordId-- record to clear ) → boolean Clears a record's bag index. Shorthand forInventoryService.setItemBagIndex with nil, used after a record has been placed into a hotbar slot.

searchDocs.title: moveToHotbar​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.moveToHotbar( player: Player ,-- inventory owner payload: Actions.InventoryMoveToHotbarPayload-- recordId and target slotIndex ) → boolean Moves an item from the bag into a specific hotbar slot. Backs the drag-drop flow from the client. Validates the slot is in range and the record is genuinely owned, then: Clears the record's current slot, if it already sat in the hotbar. If the target slot is occupied, evicts the sitting item to the bag by clearing its slot and giving it a fresh InventoryService.getNextBagIndex. Places the moving record into the target slot and clears its bagIndex. Every step is rolled back on failure — the evicted item is restored to the slot it was pushed out of — so a partial move never leaves two items sharing a slot or an item holding both indexes.

searchDocs.title: moveToInventory​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.moveToInventory( player: Player ,-- inventory owner payload: Actions.HotbarMoveToInventoryPayload-- recordId to demote ) → boolean Moves an item out of the hotbar and back into the bag: clears itsslotIndex, then assigns it the next free InventoryService.getNextBagIndex so it lands at the end of the bag.

searchDocs.title: swapSlots​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.swapSlots( player: Player ,-- inventory owner payload: Actions.HotbarSwapSlotsPayload-- fromSlotIndex and toSlotIndex ) → boolean Swaps the occupants of two hotbar slots. Both indexes must be in range and distinct, and the source slot must hold an item; the destination may be empty, in which case this is a plain move. The destination item is unslotted first so the source can claim its slot without tripping the InventoryService.setItemSlot occupancy check, then it takes the vacated source slot. If that final placement fails, both records are restored to their original slots. Only slotIndex is touched — neither item gains a bagIndex.

searchDocs.title: swapBagSlots​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.swapBagSlots( player: Player ,-- inventory owner payload: Actions.InventorySwapBagSlotsPayload-- fromRecordId and toRecordId ) → boolean Swap two bag items by their recordIds. Each item must already have abagIndex (i.e. live in the bag, not the hotbar). The bagIndexes are swapped in place — no slotIndex is touched, so neither item enters the hotbar as a side effect. Rejects the swap when the two ids are equal, when either record is missing, when either record currently sits in the hotbar (slotIndex set), or when either lacks a bagIndex. Because it is a pure exchange of two existing indexes it cannot create a collision and needs no rollback path.

searchDocs.title: sellItem​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.sellItem( player: Player ,-- seller payload: InventoryTypes.InventorySellItemPayload-- recordId and quantity ) → () Sells a quantity from a single record and credits the player. Independent of InventoryService.processSellTransaction — this path applies BoostData.modifyValueWithBoosts and then the record's own props to the base resale value, and credits exactly once. Unlike the sell-all path it does compensate on failure, re-adding the sold quantity when the coin credit fails. Replies to the client with ITEM_SELL_SUCCESS or ITEM_SELL_ERROR rather than returning a status.

searchDocs.title: sellAllItems​
searchDocs.content: </> InventoryService.sellAllItems( player: Player ,-- seller payload: InventoryTypes.InventorySellAllPayload-- the items to sell ) → () Sells a batch of records in one transaction viaInventoryService.processSellTransaction, then replies to the client with ITEM_SELL_SUCCESS (carrying soldAll and the coin total) or ITEM_SELL_ERROR. Inherits the no-rollback caveat documented onInventoryService.processSellTransaction. A batch with any blocked or malformed line (a starter item, say) is refused whole and sells nothing.

searchDocs.title: apply​
searchDocs.content: </> ItemSlotIcon.apply( icon: ImageLabel ,-- The slot's icon label nameLabel: TextLabel ,-- The slot's name label, expanded when there is no icon iconAsset: string?-- Icon asset id, or nil/empty for the no-icon layout ) → () Points a slot's icon at iconAsset, or — when the asset is empty by ItemSlotIcon.isEmpty — hides the icon and expands the name label to fill the cell. On its first call for a given label it stashes the label's Size, Position and AnchorPoint in OriginalSize / OriginalPosition / OriginalAnchorPoint attributes, and restores from those when an icon is present again. That is what makes the switch reversible, so a slot can be re-bound to a different item at any time. CAUTION The stash happens on first call, so call this before mutating the label's geometry yourself — otherwise the "original" captured is already the modified one.

searchDocs.title: configureKnife​
searchDocs.content: </> ItemProcessor.configureKnife( knife: Accessory ,-- accessory to style; must contain a Handle data: ItemTypes.BaseItem?-- item config overriding the defaults ) → () Styles a knife accessory in place, overlaying the item's config ontodefaultKnife and backfilling any key the item omits. searchDocs.title: setPropKnife​
searchDocs.content: </> ItemProcessor.setPropKnife( player: Player ,-- character owner data: ItemTypes.BaseItem?-- item config, including props.propGrip ) → () Attaches the holstered "PropKnife" accessory to the player's character, replacing any existing one. searchDocs.title: PropItem​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PropItem { rarity: RarityData.Rarity-- Required for props, unlike on BaseItem buildTime: number?-- Seconds the prop takes to build upgrades: {PropUpgradeInfo}?-- Levels this prop can be upgraded through useUpgradePrompt: boolean?-- Show the upgrade prompt when a player is nearby immovable: boolean?-- Disables the move tool for this prop destructionPrice: number?-- Cost to remove the prop, if set destroyTime: number?-- Seconds the prop takes to destroy stashable: boolean?-- Prop can be stashed back into the player's inventory propDisplayPaths: {{ path: string, label: string, formatter: ((any) → string)? }}?-- Stats surfaced on the nearby-prop display } A BaseItem that can be placed on a base. Lookup walks the current level's upgrade info down to level 1 for a value; if the next level also defines that path, the display shows "currentValue -> nextValue". destructionPrice is inert The destructionPrice field and the FeatureFlags.ChargeForDestruction flag that would govern it both exist, but nothing in the codebase currently reads either one. Removing a prop is free today.

searchDocs.title: registerCallback​
searchDocs.content: </> MarketplaceData.registerCallback( event: MarketplaceEvent,-- filter deciding which products this handles callback: ( Types.ReceiptInfo, Types.DevProduct, any, Player ) → boolean?-- fulfilment, truthy on success ) → () Registers a fulfilment callback for products matching event. When a receipt is processed, MarketplaceService runs every callback whose filter matches the product — registration order, no short-circuiting. A callback returning a falsy value fails the whole receipt, which is then left NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries it later; grants must therefore be idempotent. The callback receives the receipt, the product definition, any pending purchase data staged for that product/player pair, and the player. searchDocs.title: MinigameData
searchDocs.content: MinigameData This item only works when running on the server. Serverdormant The minigame registry. Built once at require time and frozen, it is the single source of truth for which modes and maps exist. Modes Every ModuleScript under Features/Minigames/GameModes is required and keyed by its config.name — not by its module name, which is why VotePoolItem.gameMode carries a display name rather than a path. Modules with no config, or with config.disabled set, are skipped, so a mode is taken out of rotation by flipping one field rather than by moving the file. Missing maps is an assertion rather than a skip: a mode that has been written but cannot be played is a mistake worth failing loudly on. Maps Every Model under ServerStorage.Maps is registered, keyed by its Config.displayName if it has one and its instance name otherwise. Each map must have a Spawns child — asserted, since a map without spawns cannot be played. Its Config Configuration is flattened into the map record (both value objects and attributes), a map with no Config is warned about and dropped, and a missing thumbnail falls back to a placeholder with a note. Two frozen tables come out: modes (name → GameMode) and maps (name → Map). Gated by FeatureFlags.Minigames — disabled by default; per-project forks enable it deliberately. With the flag off the module returns immediately with both tables empty and frozen, so no mode module is ever required and no map is validated. Callers see an empty registry rather than an error.

searchDocs.title: PetController
searchDocs.content: PetController This item only works when running on the client. Client Renders every player's equipped pets on this client. The server publishes each player's pet ids in their EquippedPets attribute (CosmeticService). Pets here are anchored, collision-free clones moved every frame, so they cost the server nothing and never push anyone. Ground pets trail their owner like a dog: they ease toward a formation slot behind the owner, stand on the floor found by a raycast under that slot, and hop while moving. Flying pets hover at the same slot with a slow bob. Pets hide while their owner's character is in a round (RoundTag), so they never give away where someone is hiding. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. The module waits for that value to exist. Any other value warns once and leaves all three flags false. isProduction is true when game.GameId is GameData.liveExperienceId. The three ids then come from the live set in GameData, otherwise from the dev set. placeId is always the starter place, in a Level place too. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. Death is handled once per character: ragdoll the corpse into the game container (retained in-world when the character carriesKeepRagdollInWorld), wait RESPAWN_TIME, then respawn back at origin.
