searchDocs.content: </> interface Prop { propId: string-- Unique id for this placed prop instance propItemId: string-- Item id the prop was placed from (key into Props) plotId: string-- Plot the prop sits on baseId: string-- Base the plot belongs to ownerId: number-- UserId of the base owner _allowedClientFunctions: {string}-- Method names the client may invoke boundingBox: BasePart -- Collision/query volume; authored on the server, streamed to the client Moved: Signal-- Fires after the model finishes moving to a new origin (client) Destroyed: Signal-- Fires once when the prop is torn down on either realm serverReplica: ReplicaServer?-- Authoritative state (server only) savedPropData: SavedPropData?-- Persisted record this prop was loaded from (server only) itemRecord: ItemRecord?-- Inventory record consumed to place it; nil when loaded from save positionData: PositionData?-- Grid position within the plot (server only) clientReplica: ReplicaClient?-- Read-only mirror of the server state (client only) model: Model? -- Visual model (client only) placementParticles: ParticleEmitter? -- Emitted on move, owner's client only propDisplayPaths: boolean-- Whether the prop renders path decals under it buildingProgressBar: ProgressBar?-- "Building" bar while isBuilding is set destructionProgressBar: ProgressBar?-- "Demolishing" bar while destroyStartTime is set connections: {RBXScriptConnection }-- Connections torn down with the prop } Instance shape shared by every prop. Fields are grouped by realm: a server prop has serverReplica/savedPropData and no model, a client prop has clientReplica/model and no savedPropData.

searchDocs.title: PropData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PropData { propId: string propItemId: string plotId: string baseId: string ownerId: number origin: CFrame -- World CFrame the prop should sit at serverReplica: ReplicaServer?-- Unused by new(); the server builds its own savedPropData: SavedPropData?-- Persisted record to restore from (server) itemRecord: ItemRecord?-- Inventory record being consumed (server, new placements only) initialReplicaData: {[string]: any}?-- Extra keys merged into the initial replica data positionData: PositionData?-- Grid position within the plot (server) clientReplica: ReplicaClient?-- Required on the client _boundingBox: BasePart? -- Required on the client; supplied by PropController } Construction payload for PropBaseClass.new. Subclasses use initialReplicaData to seed their own replica keys in the same dispatch that creates the replica, instead of writing them immediately afterwards.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass.new( propData: PropData,-- Identity, placement and realm-specific handles props: {[string]: any}?-- Extra fields for the subclass instance ) → Prop Constructs a new Prop instance and immediately initializes the realm-specific half of it — PropBaseClass:InitServer on the server, PropBaseClass:InitClient on the client. Subclasses call this and re-setmetatable the result onto themselves: local self = setmetatable( PropBaseClass.new(propData, { _allowedClientFunctions = { "HarvestCrop" }, Harvested = Signal.new(), }) :: any, Soil ) :: Soil props is copied onto the instance verbatim with one exception: _allowedClientFunctions is merged into the base allowlist rather than replacing it, so subclasses keep CompleteBuilding for free.

searchDocs.title: GetData​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetData() → PropReplicaData Returns the prop's current replica data, reading from whichever replica this realm owns. Both realms see the same shape and (modulo replication latency) the same values. Errors if the prop somehow has no replica — that is a construction bug, not a recoverable state.

searchDocs.title: GetSavedProps​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetSavedProps() → {[string]: any} Returns the prop's persisted, prop-specific state — the props table on the replica. Callable from either realm; reads whichever replica exists here. This is the table that gets written back to the player's datastore, so subclasses keep their durable state (crops, animals, drops) inside it rather than as plain instance fields. Errors if the prop has no replica.

searchDocs.title: GetSavedProp​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetSavedProp( key: string-- Key within the persisted props table ) → any Reads a single key out of PropBaseClass:GetSavedProps. Callable from either realm.

searchDocs.title: IsOwner​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:IsOwner( player: Player? -- Defaults to the local player on the client ) → boolean Returns whether player owns the base this prop sits on. The player argument is optional on the client only, where it defaults to Players.LocalPlayer. On the server, omitting it returns false — there is no sensible default, and silently answering true would defeat the ownership checks that allow-listed client-callable methods rely on.

searchDocs.title: GetLevel​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetLevel() → number Returns the prop's current upgrade level, read from the replica. Levels start at 1. Callable from either realm.

searchDocs.title: DispatchRemoteEvent​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> PropBaseClass:DispatchRemoteEvent( eventName: string,-- Name of the server method to invoke ...: any-- Arguments forwarded after the player argument ) → () Asks the server to run one of this prop's methods. Dispatches a PROP_REMOTE_INPUT action carrying propId, the method name and the varargs. The server looks the prop up and hands the action to PropBaseClass:_processRemoteInput, which rejects any name that is not in _allowedClientFunctions. self:DispatchRemoteEvent("HarvestCrop", cropId) Fire-and-forget: there is no reply channel. Observe the result by watching the replica.

searchDocs.title: SetSavedProp​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> PropBaseClass:SetSavedProp( key: string, value: any-- Pass nil to clear the key ) → () Writes one key into the persisted props table and republishes the whole table through the replica, which is what notifies the client.

searchDocs.title: SetSavedProps​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> PropBaseClass:SetSavedProps( newProps: {[string]: any}-- Keys to merge in ) → () Merges several keys into the persisted props table in a single replica write. Keys absent from newProps are left alone.

searchDocs.title: MoveTo​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> PropBaseClass:MoveTo( newCFrame: CFrame ,-- New world origin (bottom-centre of the prop) newPositionData: PositionData-- New plot-relative grid position ) → () Relocates the prop. Called by the Base class once it has validated a move request (grid snapping, plot bounds, hitbox intersection) — this method does no validation of its own. No-ops when newPositionData is grid-equal to the prop's current position, so a rotation-only move still goes through but a redundant one does not. Moves the server bounding box directly and publishes origin and positionData on the replica; each client then animates its own model via PropBaseClass:_localMove.

searchDocs.title: AllowClientFunction​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> PropBaseClass:AllowClientFunction( functionName: string-- Name of a method on this prop ) → () Adds a method name to this prop instance's client-callable allowlist at runtime. Warns and no-ops if it is already present. Most subclasses do not need this — they pass _allowedClientFunctions in the props table of PropBaseClass.new instead, which merges into the base allowlist. Use this only when the set of callable methods depends on runtime state. The allowlist controls what may be called, never by whom: the target method still has to check PropBaseClass:IsOwner itself.

searchDocs.title: CompleteBuilding​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> PropBaseClass:CompleteBuilding( player: Player? -- The player completing the building, if client-driven ) → () Finishes construction: clears buildStartTime from the persisted props and sets isBuilding to false, which the client picks up to drop the tint, fence and progress bar. This is on the base allowlist, so the owner's client calls it overPropBaseClass:DispatchRemoteEvent when its local build timer elapses. It is also called directly by PropBaseClass:InitServer (with no player) for builds that finished while the owner was offline. Asserts ownership when a player is supplied. A call made before the saved build window has passed finishes the build when the window ends instead.

searchDocs.title: ShowOutline​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> PropBaseClass:ShowOutline( show: boolean-- true to show, false to tear down ) → () Shows or hides the selection treatment on the prop — used while the prop is picked up in edit mode, and cleared when demolition starts. Two parts, both owned by an internal Maid so hiding is a single Destroy(): the model's own Outline child (if it has one) has its parts faded in, and a bobbing, slowly rotating arrow is cloned into the Workspace above the prop. The arrow's height is recomputed every RenderStep so it tracks a prop that is being dragged. Calling it again with true replaces the previous outline rather than stacking a second one.

searchDocs.title: GetCurrentLevelInfo​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetCurrentLevelInfo() → ( ItemTypes.PropUpgradeInfo?, number? ) Returns the upgrade record describing the prop's current level, plus that level number. Callable from either realm. The upgrades list is 1-indexed from level 2 — index n describes the upgrade into level n + 1 — so the current level's record is upgrades[level - 1]. A level-1 prop therefore returns nil for the record: level 1 is the item's own base stats, not an upgrade.

searchDocs.title: GetNextLevelInfo​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:GetNextLevelInfo() → ( ItemTypes.PropUpgradeInfo?, number? ) Returns the upgrade record for the next level (upgrades[level]) and that level's number, or nil when the prop is already maxed or the item defines no upgrades. Callable from either realm. Used both as a "can this be upgraded at all?" test and as the source of the price shown on the upgrade prompt.

searchDocs.title: ShowInfo​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> PropBaseClass:ShowInfo() → () Attaches the persistent PropInfo billboard (item name and current level) to the model and keeps the level label in sync with the replica. Opt-in per subclass rather than automatic — Town turns it on in its constructor, most props do not. There is no matching hide; the billboard lives until PropBaseClass:Destroy.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> PropBaseClass:Destroy() → () Tears the prop down on whichever realm it is called from, then firesDestroyed. Subclasses hook that signal to clean up their own state rather than overriding this method. On the client: destroys the model, both progress bars, the outline Maid, the info billboard and the upgrade prompt, and unbinds the two RenderStep hooks registered in PropBaseClass:InitClient. On the server: cancels the build timer/heartbeat, destroys the bounding box and the Replica, and removes the base's hitbox sub-container once it is empty. This does not touch persisted data — removing the prop from the player's saved base is the caller's job.

searchDocs.title: RouteDescriptor​
searchDocs.content: </> interface RouteDescriptor { path: string-- Unique key used to navigate/mount. Duplicates assert at init component: React.ComponentType<RouteProps>-- Rendered by Views with the route's props isDefault: boolean?-- Regular routes only. Starts active, cannot be unmounted isPortal: boolean?-- Renders concurrently with the active route and other portals autoMountPortal: boolean?-- Portals only. Set false to stay unmounted until asked } Declares one route. The full list lives in src/Client/App/Client.luau and is handed to Router.Provider at mount. isPortal is the important flag: portal routes render concurrently in their own slots, regular routes share a single mutually-exclusive slot. isDefault picks the regular route that is active from the first render and can never be unmounted; it is invalid on a portal.

searchDocs.title: RouterState​
searchDocs.content: </> interface RouterState { routes: {[string]: RouteDescriptor}-- Every declared route, keyed by path currentPath: string?-- The one active regular route, or nil when the slot is empty currentProps: RouteProps?-- Props for the active regular route mountedPortals: {[string]: RouteProps}-- Path -> props for each concurrently mounted portal } Everything the Router knows, rebuilt on each reducer transition and published through Provider.StateContext.

searchDocs.title: NavigationApi​
searchDocs.content: </> interface NavigationApi { navigate: ( path: string, props: RouteProps? ) → boolean-- Swap the regular-route slot mount: ( path: string, props: RouteProps? ) → boolean-- Mount a portal (or navigate, for a regular route) unmount: (path: string) → boolean-- Unmount a portal, or clear the regular-route slot navigateToDefault: () → boolean-- Navigate to the isDefault route, if one exists } The imperative half of the Router, obtained with Router.useNavigation(). Every method is a dispatch wrapper and returns immediately — the boolean reports that the action was dispatched, not that the transition was valid. Rejected transitions surface as a warn from the reducer. navigateToDefault is the exception: it scans the descriptor list itself and returns false when no route is flagged isDefault.

searchDocs.content: </> ScaleTween.ScaleTween( model: Model ,-- Model to scale startScale: number?,-- Starting scale (defaults to 0.1) targetScale: number?,-- Target scale (defaults to 1) tweenInfo: TweenInfo? -- Custom duration and easing instead of the default ) → RBXScriptConnection -- Disconnect to stop early Scales model from startScale to targetScale and returns the RBXScriptConnection driving it — disconnect it to stop the tween early, leaving the model at whatever scale it reached. searchDocs.title: ScalingButton
searchDocs.content: ScalingButton This item only works when running on the client. Client Watcher for the ScalingButton tag: gives any legacy GuiButton a hover-grow and press-shrink animation without a line of code per button. Registered by CollectionWatcherController at boot. Tag a button in Studio and it animates; nothing else is required. Behavior MouseEnter — tweens to HoverScale (default 1.2) of the button's original size, over TweenInTime MouseLeave — back to the original size, over TweenOutTime InputBegan with MouseButton1 or Touch — down to ActivatedScale (default 0.9), over TweenInTime InputEnded — back to the hover size if the pointer is still over the button, otherwise the original size, over InputEndTweenTime Enter and press are both gated on button.Active, so an inactive button stays inert. Leave and release are not, so a button deactivated mid-hover still settles back. Every branch skips the tween when the button is already at the target size. Only the Scale components of the button's UDim2 are multiplied — Offset is left alone, so buttons sized in pixels do not animate. Attributes All optional, read once per button when the handler first runs. Changing them afterwards has no effect. Attribute Default HoverScale 1.2 ActivatedScale 0.9 TweenTime 0.1 — the fallback for the three below TweenInTime TweenTime TweenOutTime TweenTime InputEndTweenTime TweenOutTime NOTE The original size is captured on first run, so a button whose size is driven by something else after registration will animate around a stale base. This watcher only covers legacy rbxmx buttons; React buttons handle their own hover states. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. All rights reserved. firebit/murder-escape - proprietary and confidential.

searchDocs.title: generateStock​
searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.generateStock() → {[string]: {[string]: number}}-- shopType -> itemId -> quantity Computes the stock every shop should be holding right now and writes it into the shop replicas. For each item it finds the most recent restock time that should have occurred (floor(now / restockInterval) * restockInterval) and refills to maxStockQuantity only when that moment lies inside the current global restock window; otherwise the existing quantity is carried forward. Replicas are only written when something actually changed, so an idle cycle costs no replication.

searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.applyStock( stockByShop: {[string]: {[string]: number}}-- shopType -> itemId -> quantity ) → () Writes a previously computed stock table back onto the shop replicas, clamping quantities at zero. Unknown shops and unknown items are skipped, and replicas are only touched when a quantity actually changed. Used by ShopService.initializeStock to restore in-memory stock rather than regenerating it.

Items with no ownershipLimit (or a limit of 0) are unlimited and always pass. Counting differs by item type: Skin — an [ItemRecord] in profile.inventory like everything else, but treated as a boolean unlock via CosmeticService.ownsSkin. Prop — inventory quantity plus any props the player has already placed in the world. That second term currently always reads zero: the BaseService dependency is a local stub pending the Base system port. everything else — the summed quantity of matching inventory records.

searchDocs.title: purchase​
searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.purchase( player: Player ,-- buyer itemId: string,-- item to buy quantity: number?-- asserted positive; not otherwise honoured ) → boolean Buys a non-stocked item with soft currency. Rejects anything hidden, unpriced, or carrying stockData — stocked items go through ShopService.purchaseStock instead. Checks the ownership limit and the balance, debits via CurrencyService.take, logs a Sink resource event, then grants one copy. Note that quantity is asserted positive but is otherwise unused: exactly one item is charged for and granted.

searchDocs.title: purchaseStock​
searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.purchaseStock( player: Player ,-- buyer shopType: string,-- what shop the player is buying from itemId: string,-- item to buy quantity: number?-- amount, defaults to 1; priced per unit ) → boolean Buys an item from a specific shop, honouring stock when scarcity is enabled. The order of operations is: validate the item, check the ownership limit, verify the balance, debit the currency, then attempt the stock decrement. Because payment happens before the stock check, a failed decrement is compensated by an explicit refund (logged as a Refund resource event) rather than avoided. The stock decrement only runs when both hold: FeatureFlags.ScarcityShop is on and the item declares stockData. With the flag off (the default) the branch is skipped entirely and stock is effectively infinite. Skins are handled by CosmeticService.markPurchased instead of [ShopService.giveItemToPlayer]: they're recorded as a boolean unlock, not a stackable quantity, and are auto-equipped and applied to both the character and the held item.

searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.getRestockInfo() → table-- { globalRefresh = {...}, shops = { [shopType] = { [itemId] = {...} } } } Builds a debug snapshot of restock timing: the global refresh interval and the time left on it, plus per-shop, per-item restock interval, time remaining and current quantity. modulus on each entry is the elapsed time within that interval, which is what the scheduling comparisons key off. searchDocs.title: manualRestock​
searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.manualRestock( shopType: string-- key in ShopData.SHOPS ) → boolean-- whether anything actually restocked Force-restocks a single shop, used at boot so items are available immediately rather than after the first scheduled window. Differs from the scheduled path in what it guarantees: items ofINITIAL_STOCK_RARITY ("Common") and all props are filled to maxStockQuantity unconditionally, while rarer items only restock if their own interval boundary is within the last second — and even then they refill to 0 rather than their max, so rare stock is never seeded at boot. The code is upper-cased before lookup. Otherwise the redemption is written to the redeemed_codes DataStore first — the grant only happens if that write succeeds, so a datastore failure cannot produce a free duplicate. searchDocs.content: </> ShopService.init() → () Boots the service: binds the Handlers folder, and registers the item developer-product callback so a purchased item is granted through InventoryService once the receipt is processed. The shop stock machinery — replica setup, item population, initial stock, the per-shop boot restock and the restock loop — is entirely behindFeatureFlags.ScarcityShop, which is off by default. searchDocs.title: SkillTreeData
searchDocs.content: SkillTreeData Permanent coin-bought upgrade tree (the lobby SkillTree modal). Nodes form a radial skill tree: 3 themed branches wind out from a decorative hub, each branch INTERLEAVING its stats round-robin (health, regen, health, regen, …) so a player can never max one stat without buying the tiers of its branch-mates along the way. Each node grants +1 effect tier of its stat and requires only the previous node in its branch (a pure chain). Owned nodes persist in the profile (skillNodes map, string keys). The effective permanent level of a stat is the count of owned nodes granting it (see statLevels); the game applies the actual effect magnitudes. The placeholder stats below are generic — a game forking this tree replaces STATS and BRANCHES with its own content. The schema (node ids, costs, prerequisites, layout) is the product. Node positions are canvas-scale coordinates for SkillTreeModal (they may exceed 0..1 — the canvas is a coordinate space, panning reaches them); layout is generated here so the tree can be re-shaped in data alone. Node ids stay {stat}_{tier}, so profiles survive topology changes.

searchDocs.title: SkillTreeService
searchDocs.content: SkillTreeService Permanent skill upgrade tree — a persistent coin sink. Lobby only: players buy SkillTreeData nodes with coins; owned nodes save to profile.skillNodes and replicate to the client through the normal profile replica (the tree UI reads ClientState.playerData.skillNodes). Prerequisites are validated server-side (SkillTreeData.canBuy) — a client asking for a node whose parents aren't owned is rejected before any coins move. Effects are applied by the game's own systems, which read owned nodes via getOwned (or levels via SkillTreeData.statLevels). Gated behind FeatureFlags.SkillTree: with it off, init binds no handlers, so BUY_SKILL_NODE gets no reply.

searchDocs.title: Crop​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Crop { model: Model -- The instantiated model for the current life stage cropLifeStage: CropLifeStage-- Stage the current model represents cropData: CropTypes.SavedCropData-- Reference to the replicated record instantlyGrown: boolean-- Pinned to Mature by an instant-grow purchase position: CFrame -- World origin, recomputed when the prop moves progressBar: ProgressBar?-- Growth bar; removed once mature prompt: ProximityPrompt? -- Instant-grow, harvest, or steal prompt attachment: Attachment -- Anchor on the soil model that prompts/UI hang off cropAttachments: {Attachment }-- Produce mount points on a mature tree model spawnedProduce: {[Attachment ]: { savedData: CropTypes.ProduceData, cropPart: BasePart , harvestPrompt: ProximityPrompt? }}-- Produce currently rendered on this tree isTree: boolean-- Whether the seed defines cropTreeData } Client-side view of one planted crop: the instances currently rendered for it, paired with the server record they were built from. Lives in Soil.crops and is reconciled against the replica every RenderStep. Server-side Soils have no Crop objects at all.

searchDocs.title: GrowthData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface GrowthData { flowersAt: number-- Server time the crop enters the Flower stage maturesAt: number-- Server time the crop becomes harvestable wiltsAt: number?-- Server time it wilts; nil when the seed never wilts cropLifeStage: CropLifeStage-- Stage as of the moment this was computed } Point-in-time snapshot of a crop's growth, computed from its plantedAt and the seed's timings. Recomputed on demand rather than cached, so it is always consistent with the server clock (Workspace:GetServerTimeNow()) on both realms.

searchDocs.title: Soil​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Soil { clientReplica: ReplicaClient-- Replica narrowed to props: SavedSoilData (client) serverReplica: ReplicaServer-- Replica narrowed to props: SavedSoilData (server) Harvested: Signal-- (soil, cropData, harvestTime) — a whole crop was taken HarvestedBulk: Signal-- (soil, { BulkCropDataItem }) — HarvestAllCrops finished HarvestedProduce: Signal-- (soil, produceData, cropId, harvestTime) — one tree produce was taken HarvestReady: Signal-- (soil, cropData) — a crop just became harvestable (client) cleanup: Maid?-- Owns every connection made by this Soil crops: {Crop}?-- Rendered crops (client only) scaleModifier: number-- Multiplier applied to new crop and produce scale } Instance shape of a Soil, on top of everything inherited from PropBaseClass. Harvested fires on both realms but means slightly different things: on the server it fires from Soil:Harvest as the authoritative event that the economy layer credits the player from; on the client it fires from the reconciliation pass whenever a crop disappears from replicated data, and is used for local VFX/SFX only.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Soil.new(propData: PropData) → Soil Creates a Soil prop. Seeds the replica's props from savedPropData when the plot is being restored from a save (and with an empty crop list otherwise), then hands off to PropBaseClass.new with the four harvest signals and the HarvestCrop/HarvestProduce client allowlist. Realm-specific setup afterwards: Client — allocates crops, starts the reconciliation loop (Soil:_setupCropModels), and re-pivots every crop when the prop is moved. Server — starts the tree produce timer (Soil:_startProduceTimers). Both realms recompute Soil:_setScaleModifier on every level change.

searchDocs.title: CreateProgressBar​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Soil:CreateProgressBar( parent: Instance ,-- Anchor for the billboard cropName: string,-- Label shown on the bar growthPercentage: number-- Initial fill, 0..1 ) → ProgressBar.ProgressBar Builds a growth ProgressBar hosted in a fresh BillboardGui parented to parent (normally the crop's attachment). The bar is offset slightly below the anchor so it sits at the base of the crop rather than through it. The caller owns the result and must dispose of it with the module-localdestroyProgressBar helper, which destroys the BillboardGui as well — calling ProgressBar:Destroy() alone leaks the billboard.

searchDocs.title: CreateNewCropEntry​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Soil:CreateNewCropEntry( cropData: CropTypes.SavedCropData,-- Replicated crop record offset: CropTypes.CropOffset-- Plot-relative position and rotation ) → Crop? Instantiates everything a newly replicated crop needs and returns the Crop bookkeeping entry for it: the stage model, an Attachment on the soil model that prompts and UI hang off (raised 2 studs so prompts float above the crop), a growth ProgressBar when the crop is neither mature nor instantly grown, and — for a mature tree — its produce mount points. Returns nil when the seed no longer resolves, the model has not been built yet, or the offset falls outside the plot. Callers treat nil as "skip this frame". This only builds instances; the caller inserts the result into self.crops and attaches the appropriate prompt.

searchDocs.title: AddSeed​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:AddSeed( seedItemId: string,-- Item id of the seed to plant offset: Vector2 -- Plot-relative X/Z offset in studs ) → () Plants a seed at a plot-relative offset. Silently no-ops (with a warning only for an unknown seed) if the seed id is not a seed, the offset is outside the plot, or the spot is too close to an existing crop — the client is expected to have pre-checked withSoil:CanPlantAtOffset, so a rejection here means a stale preview or a tampered request. Rolls the crop's random rotation, scale (from BaseData.CROP_SCALE_RANGE, multiplied by the plot's scaleModifier) and visual modifier at plant time, then appends it to props.crops and republishes. Consuming the seed from the player's inventory is the caller's responsibility.

searchDocs.title: CanPlantAtOffset​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:CanPlantAtOffset( offset: Vector2 -- Plot-relative X/Z offset in studs ) → boolean Whether a seed could be planted at offset right now — bounds and spacing combined. Exactly the checks Soil:AddSeed performs, exposed so a caller can test without attempting the plant.

searchDocs.title: GetCropById​
searchDocs.content: </> Soil:GetCropById(cropId: string) → CropTypes.SavedCropData? Looks up a planted crop's record by its cropId, reading whichever replica this realm owns. Returns nil if no crop matches — which is the normal result after the crop has been harvested. The returned table is the live record, not a copy: mutating it and then republishing props is how Soil:InstantGrowCrop works.

searchDocs.title: InstantGrowCrop​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:InstantGrowCrop( cropId: string-- Crop to grow ) → () Marks a single crop instantlyGrown, pinning it to the Mature stage regardless of elapsed time. Called after the player buys the grow_crop developer product from the crop's instant-grow prompt. Warns and no-ops if the crop id, its seed, or the seed's maturityTime cannot be resolved.

searchDocs.title: GrowAllCrops​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:GrowAllCrops() → () Instantly matures every crop on the plot. Backs the base's "Grow All" point. Normal crops are simply flagged instantlyGrown. Trees additionally have their produce topped up to a full set of CropAttachment slots — existing produce has its creationTime zeroed so it reads as ripe, and missing slots are filled with already-ripe produce — while still respecting the tree's lifetime produceYield.

searchDocs.title: HarvestAllCrops​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:HarvestAllCrops() → () Harvests everything harvestable on the plot in one pass and firesHarvestedBulk with the collected items. Backs the base's "Harvest All" point. Iterates backwards so removals do not disturb the traversal. Per crop: Trees yield all their current produce and keep standing, with their produce list emptied; a tree that has exhausted its produceYield is removed from the plot at this point, since it can never bear again. Normal crops yield once and are removed, but only if mature or instantly grown — immature crops are left alone. Unlike Soil:Harvest this fires a single bulk signal rather than one Harvested per crop, so the economy layer can credit the whole haul in one transaction.

searchDocs.title: Harvest​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:Harvest( cropId: string-- Crop to harvest ) → () Harvests one crop: removes it from props.crops, republishes, and fires Harvested with the crop record and how long past maturity it was taken. That signal is the authoritative event the economy layer credits from. Refuses (with a warning) if the crop id is unknown or the crop is neither mature nor instantly grown. This is the unguarded internal path — it performs no ownership check. Client-initiated harvests go through Soil:HarvestCrop, which checks ownership and then delegates here.

searchDocs.title: HarvestCrop​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:HarvestCrop( player: Player ,-- The requesting client cropId: string?-- Crop to harvest; a missing id warns and no-ops ) → () Client-callable entry point for harvesting one crop — allow-listed in_allowedClientFunctions, so it is reached via DispatchRemoteEvent, never called directly. Verifies the caller owns the plot, resolves the crop, confirms it is harvestable, then delegates to Soil:Harvest. A request for a crop that is not yet mature is dropped rather than errored — the intent is to surface a "buy instant grow?" upsell there, which is not implemented yet.

searchDocs.title: HarvestProduce​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Soil:HarvestProduce( player: Player ,-- The requesting client produceId: string?,-- Produce to take cropId: string?-- Tree the produce belongs to ) → () Client-callable entry point for harvesting a single piece of tree produce — allow-listed in _allowedClientFunctions. Verifies ownership, locates the produce within its parent crop, removes it, republishes and fires HarvestedProduce. The tree itself is untouched and will grow the slot back on its next produce tick; the tree is only ever removed by Soil:HarvestAllCrops once its produceYield is spent.

searchDocs.title: Path​
searchDocs.content: </> type Path = string | number How a sound is addressed: a dotted SoundService path, an asset id number, or an rbxassetid:// string.

searchDocs.title: SoundOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundOptions { volume: number-- Overrides the sound's volume loop: boolean-- Sets Looped } Overrides applied after the sound is resolved. Both are only applied when truthy, so volume = 0 and loop = false leave the existing value alone.

searchDocs.title: get​
searchDocs.content: </> Sounds.get( path: Path,-- Sound to resolve options: SoundOptions?-- Volume and loop overrides ) → Sound?  Resolves path to a Sound without playing it, or returns nil if nothing matches. The result is not parented, so parent it (or call Sounds.play) before it will be audible — except for tree paths, which return the already-parented shared instance.

searchDocs.title: play​
searchDocs.content: </> Sounds.play( path: Path,-- Sound to play options: SoundOptions?-- Volume and loop overrides ) → Sound?  Resolves path and plays it immediately, returning the Sound so the caller can stop it or wait on Ended. Returns nil when the path does not resolve — a missing sound is not an error. Nothing is cleaned up for you; a non-looping sound created from an asset id is left for the garbage collector once you drop the reference. Sounds.play("UI.Click") Sounds.play(1234567, { volume = 0.5, loop = true })

searchDocs.title: use​
searchDocs.content: </> Sounds.use( path: Path,-- Sound to resolve options: SoundOptions?-- Volume and loop overrides ) → ( () → ()?, Sound? )-- Play callback and the resolved sound Hook-style variant: resolves the sound once and returns a play callback alongside it, so a component can prepare a sound at mount and trigger it on demand. Returns nothing at all when the path does not resolve, so destructure defensively. local playClick = Sounds.use("UI.Click") button.Activated:Connect(function() if playClick then playClick() end end)

searchDocs.title: spawnParticle​
searchDocs.content: </> spawnParticle.spawnParticle(data: { name: string | {string}, source: Vector3 | CFrame | BasePart | Model , size: Vector3 | number?, lifetime: number?, emission: number?, emissionTime: number? }) → Maid.Maid-- Owns the emitters and any anchor part created for them Emits one or more named particle effects at source. source may be a BasePart or Model to parent the emitters to (models use their PrimaryPart), or a Vector3/CFrame, in which case an invisible anchor part is created in Workspace and cleaned up with the rest. By default each emitter fires a single burst via ParticleEmitter:Emit(). Passing emissionTime instead leaves the emitter enabled for that many seconds, and extends the cleanup delay to match. Everything is tracked by the returned [Maid] and destroyed automatically once the effect's lifetime is up; destroy the maid yourself to cut the effect short. spawnParticle({ name = { "Impact.Sparks", "Impact.Smoke" }, source = hit.Position, emission = 40, })

searchDocs.title: Update​
searchDocs.content: </> Spring:Update(deltaTime: number) → T Updates the spring. This method should be called continuously, even if the target value hasn't changed. local newValue = spring:Update(deltaTime)

searchDocs.title: SetTarget​
searchDocs.content: </> Spring:SetTarget(target: T) → () Points the spring at a new target. Setting a target that differs from the current one also zeroes the velocity, so the spring eases into the new target from rest rather than carrying momentum from the previous one. Setting the same target again is a no-op.

searchDocs.title: Impulse​
searchDocs.content: </> Spring:Impulse(velocity: T) → () Impulses the spring. spring:Impulse(rng:NextUnitVector() * 10)

searchDocs.title: Reset​
searchDocs.content: </> Spring:Reset(value: T) → () Resets the spring to the given value.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> StatsController.init() → () Bootstrap hook. Seeds ClientState.coins / ClientState.xp from the profile already in ClientState.playerData, then connects to playerData.Changed to keep them in step. The seed is safe because Entry.client.luau blocks on DataController before bootstrapping controllers, so the profile is always present by the time this runs.

searchDocs.title: TeleportPad
searchDocs.content: TeleportPad This item only works when running on the client. Client Watcher for the TeleportPad tag: a BasePart that requests a teleport when the local player walks onto it. Registered by CollectionWatcherController at boot. Tag a part, give it a Node string attribute naming the destination, and it works. On touch the watcher dispatches TELEPORT_REQUEST with { nodeName = <Node> }. The teleport itself is the server's decision — this only asks. Guards Touches from other players are ignored; only Players.LocalPlayer triggers a request. A one-second per-player cooldown suppresses the repeated Touched events a character generates while standing on the pad, so a single step is a single request. A pad with no Node attribute asserts at registration rather than silently doing nothing. NOTE The cooldown table is keyed by Player even though only the local player can ever get in — a leftover from the shared-code shape. Neither the cooldown nor the touch connection is torn down on CollectionObject.Destroyed; pads live for the session. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. All rights reserved. firebit/murder-escape - proprietary and confidential.

searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: </> TrackedPlayerValues.set( player: Player , key: string,-- Value name value: any-- Value to store ) → () Stores a value under key, replacing anything already there. Silently does nothing for a player who has left.

searchDocs.title: add​
searchDocs.content: </> TrackedPlayerValues.add( player: Player , key: string,-- Value name value: number-- Amount to add ) → () Adds to a numeric value, treating an unset key as 0 — the usual way to accumulate a session counter. Silently does nothing for a player who has left.

searchDocs.content: </> TrackedPlayerValues.remove( player: Player , key: string-- Value name ) → () Clears a single tracked value, leaving the player's other values intact.

searchDocs.title: clear​
searchDocs.content: </> TrackedPlayerValues.clear(player: Player ) → () Discards everything tracked for a player. Unlike the automatic cleanup on leave, this does not fire PlayerRemoving — the values are dropped without anyone being told.

searchDocs.content: </> interface ToastData { text: string-- Message body height: number?-- Pixels; sized to the text when omitted accentColor: Color3? -- Accent bar / border color onActivated: (() → ())?-- Invoked when the toast is tapped, alongside the tap-dismiss sound: (string | false)?-- CoreSounds key played as it shows; false is silent; nil plays toast-notification } A short transient notification that stacks with other toasts.

searchDocs.title: MessageData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MessageData { header: string-- Title line body: string-- Message body timeout: number?-- Seconds before auto-dismiss; stays up when omitted } A larger titled message, for things a toast is too small to carry.

searchDocs.title: HintData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface HintData { text: string-- Hint text timeout: number?-- Seconds before it clears } A single line of guidance text, typically pinned rather than stacked.

searchDocs.title: SpeakerData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SpeakerData { name: string-- Display name shown on the dialogue box icon: string?-- Portrait image asset id chatterSoundId: string?-- Sound played per character as the text types out } Identity of whoever is talking in a DialogData. Referenced by name from the dialogue's speaker field rather than embedded, so one speaker can be reused across many lines.

searchDocs.title: DialogData​
searchDocs.content: </> interface DialogData { text: string-- Line to type out persist: boolean?-- Keep the box open after the line finishes timeAfterTypewriter: number?-- Seconds to hold the completed line before advancing speaker: string?-- Key of a SpeakerData; narration when omitted position: "top" | "bottom" | "center" | "left"?-- Where the box is anchored hideClose: boolean?-- Remove the close button hideSkip: boolean?-- Remove the skip-typewriter affordance options: {string}?-- Turns the line into a choice prompt pulsedOption: string?-- Option to highlight, e.g. during onboarding yield: boolean?-- Block the caller until the line is dismissed } One line of dialogue, optionally with choices. Setting yield makes the call block, which is what lets a scripted sequence be written as straight-line code. Supplying options turns the box into a prompt; hideClose and hideSkip are how a sequence forces the player to actually read or answer.

searchDocs.title: VehicleAttachmentData
searchDocs.content: VehicleAttachmentData Defines vehicle attachment configurations. Each attachment has a slot type, model reference, image, and optional properties like speed modifiers. Copyright (c) 2026 firebit. All rights reserved. firebit/murder-escape - proprietary and confidential.

searchDocs.title: Vehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Vehicle { car: Model -- The spawned car model driverSeat: VehicleSeat -- Required; construction fails without it passengerSeat: VehicleSeat -- Optional in practice; may be nil on a one-seat model body: BasePart -- The car's Body part locked: boolean-- While true, nobody may sit down maid: Maid-- Owns the model and every connection owner: Player? -- Whose vehicle this is; nil for a public vehicle occupiedDriver: Player? -- Current driver occupiedPassenger: Player? -- Current passenger occupiedSignal: Signal-- (player, "StartControl" | "StopControl") attachments: {[string]: Model }-- Slot type to attached model ownerOnly: boolean-- Restrict the driver's seat to owner lastSatInCar: number-- Server time of the last seat entry; debounces the prompt timerThread: thread?-- Pending idle-despawn timer } Instance shape of a server-side vehicle.

searchDocs.title: VehicleConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface VehicleConfig { owner: Player? -- Whose vehicle this is; also the reference point for auto-placement ownerOnly: boolean?-- Restrict the driver's seat to the owner (default false) spawnCFrame: CFrame? -- Explicit placement, skipping the ground/clearance search } Construction options for Vehicle.new. Supplying spawnCFrame bypasses placement resolution entirely, which is how a vehicle can be spawned somewhere no player is standing.

searchDocs.title: getCar​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle.getCar(model: Model ) → Vehicle? Recovers the Vehicle wrapper for a car model from the module cache, or nil if the model is not a live vehicle. The bridge every caller holding only a model uses to reach this class's methods.

searchDocs.title: getCarModel​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle.getCarModel() → Model  Returns the shared car template from Assets.Vehicles.Car. This is the original, not a clone — read it for bounding-box measurements, do not modify it.

searchDocs.title: getRaycastParams​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle.getRaycastParams() → RaycastParams Returns the shared raycast params used for spawn ground-finding, filtered against Spawner- and Water-tagged instances so neither counts as ground. Kept in sync as those tags come and go.

searchDocs.title: getOverlapParams​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle.getOverlapParams() → OverlapParams Returns the shared overlap params used for the spawn clearance check, filtered the same way as Vehicle.getRaycastParams and capped at one result since any single hit is enough to reject a spot.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle.new( config: VehicleConfig?-- Defaults to an unowned vehicle with no placement ) → Vehicle? Spawns a vehicle, or returns nil if it cannot be placed. Placement is either the supplied spawnCFrame or, for an owned vehicle, resolved from the owner's character: a point SPAWN_DISTANCE studs ahead is raycast down for ground, and a temporary box the size of the car's bounding box is overlap-tested for clearance. Either failing returns nil. This repeats the check VehicleController.spawn already ran on the client, because the client's answer is advisory. Setup, in order: Clone and tag the model, stamp OwnerId and a SpeedMultiplier of 1. Nudge the driver's SeatWeld via the seat attachment so the character sits at the wheel rather than at the seat part's raw origin. Wire seat Occupant listeners and the enter prompt (itself debounced to one entry per second). Assign collision groups: Details → CarDetail, DBO parts → CarBody, and every part carrying a CylindricalConstraint attachment → CarWheel with high-friction physical properties so the wheels actually grip. Parent to the Workspace, then task.defer the mass-derived suspension tuning described on Vehicle. Returns nil without side effects if the model has no DriverSeat.

searchDocs.title: StartTimer​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:StartTimer() → () Arms the idle-despawn timer, which runs DESPAWN_TIME after the vehicle is spawned or vacated. Vehicle:StopTimer cancels it when someone gets in. NOTE The timer body is commented out, so the vehicle is never actually despawned — the scheduling is live but the effect is disabled. Re-enabling it requires calling back into VehicleService, which is why it was stubbed: this class does not import that service.

searchDocs.title: StopTimer​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:StopTimer() → () Cancels a pending idle-despawn timer, if any.

searchDocs.title: OnOccupantChanged​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:OnOccupantChanged( seat: VehicleSeat -- The seat whose occupancy changed ) → () Handles a seat's Occupant changing — the voluntary-exit path, as opposed to the forced Eject* methods. The enter prompt is toggled to match occupancy, and the idle-despawn timer is stopped while someone is driving and restarted once the vehicle empties. A departing driver triggers the full handover described on [Vehicle]: fire StopControl, brake, sever the character's weld, zero the wheel velocities the client was commanding, reclaim network ownership through the un-anchor/set/re-anchor dance, place the character on the ground to the car's left, zero their velocity so they do not inherit the car's momentum, and stop the idle engine sound. A departing passenger is simply placed on the right-hand side. Either way the character's collision is restored on the way out.

searchDocs.title: EnterDriverSeat​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EnterDriverSeat(player: Player ) → () Seats a player as the driver. Refuses if the seat is taken, or if ownerOnly is set and they are not the owner. Grants the player network ownership of the assembly before seating them — this is what makes their client the physics authority, and the vehicle must be un-anchored first for the grant to take.

searchDocs.title: EnterPassengerSeat​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EnterPassengerSeat(player: Player ) → () Seats a player as the passenger. Refuses if there is no passenger seat or it is occupied. Passengers get no network ownership and no control.

searchDocs.title: getSeatedPlayers​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:getSeatedPlayers() → {Player } Every player currently seated in this vehicle: the driver (if any) followed by the passenger. Only players who boarded through the enter handlers are known — engine touch-seated characters are untracked.

searchDocs.title: AttachAttachment​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:AttachAttachment( attachmentType: string,-- Slot name; also the attachment point prefix attachmentModel: Model -- Template to clone; needs a PrimaryPart ) → boolean-- Whether it was attached Clones attachmentModel onto the vehicle at the platform attachment named <attachmentType>Attachment, welds it to the platform and records it in the slot. Refuses if the slot is already filled — VehicleService:equipAttachment removes the incumbent first — and warns and refuses if the model has no PrimaryPart or the named attachment point does not exist. Every part of the clone is put on the CarBody collision group so an attachment cannot collide with the car it is bolted to.

searchDocs.title: RemoveAttachment​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:RemoveAttachment(attachmentType: string) → boolean-- false if the slot was already empty Destroys the attachment in a slot and clears it.

searchDocs.title: GetAttachment​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:GetAttachment(attachmentType: string) → Model?  Returns the model in a slot, or nil.

searchDocs.title: GetAllAttachments​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:GetAllAttachments() → {[string]: Model } Returns the live slot-to-model map. Not a copy — do not mutate it.

searchDocs.title: SetSpeedMultiplier​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:SetSpeedMultiplier( multiplier: number-- 0..1 ) → () Sets the vehicle's SpeedMultiplier attribute, which the driving client reads every frame to scale its top speed. Using an attribute rather than a remote means the change replicates on its own and applies immediately. Clamped to 0..1, so this can only slow a vehicle down; 0 is a full stop. No-ops if the vehicle has been unparented.

searchDocs.title: Brake​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:Brake() → () Stops the vehicle by setting its speed multiplier to 0. The vehicle stays braked until something restores the multiplier — entering the driver's seat resets it to 1.

searchDocs.title: EjectDriver​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EjectDriver() → () Forcibly removes the driver, placing them off the car's left side. No-ops if there is no driver.

searchDocs.title: EjectPassenger​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EjectPassenger() → () Forcibly removes the passenger, placing them off the car's right side. No-ops if there is no passenger.

searchDocs.title: EjectAll​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EjectAll() → () Empties the vehicle — driver and passenger both.

searchDocs.title: EjectPlayer​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:EjectPlayer(player: Player ) → () Ejects one specific occupant, whichever seat they are in. No-ops if they are not aboard.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Vehicle:Destroy() → () Tears the vehicle down: cancels the despawn timer, destroys the model, and destroys the Maid — which also restores collision on any seated characters, drops the entry from the module cache and destroys occupiedSignal.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.init() → () Bootstrap hook. Adopts every existing Vehicle-tagged model and subscribes to later additions. No-ops entirely when the Vehicle feature flag is off.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.start() → () Bootstrap hook. Subscribes to VEHICLE_START_CONTROL, the action the server dispatches when this player takes or leaves the driver's seat. Taking control hides the enter prompt and starts the physics loop; releasing it does the reverse. No-ops entirely when the Vehicle feature flag is off.

searchDocs.title: setupCar​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.setupCar( car: Model -- The vehicle model to adopt ) → () Adopts car as the vehicle this client controls: resolves every instance the physics loop needs, measures the steering geometry, resets all motion state, and wires the lifetime listeners. Expects a specific model layout — DriverSeat, Chasis/Platform/Engine, the four Cylindrical* wheel motors on the engine, SpringAttachmentF* on the platform, and a Flight folder holding the submarine constraints. Every lookup is a WaitForChild, so a model missing any of these hangs here rather than erroring. Steering geometry is derived from the live attachment positions rather than hard-coded: track width from the two front spring attachments, wheelbase from front-left to rear-left. Both use Magnitude, so they hold regardless of how the model is oriented when this runs. The car is un-anchored at the end — models are spawned anchored so they cannot drift before their constraints are configured. The initial state is chosen from the character's Swimming attribute, and a listener keeps it in sync afterwards. Transitions out of water deliberately wait 0.4s (guarded by switchingState) so the vehicle does not snap back to driving mode while it is still breaching the surface. Yields on the WaitForChild calls.

searchDocs.title: setState​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.setState( state: VehicleTypes.CarState-- "driving" or "submarine" ) → () Switches the vehicle between driving and submarine. No-ops if already in that state. The two modes are mutually exclusive by construction: the four flight constraints are enabled only for submarine, and wheel MotorMaxTorque is set to the full torque for driving and to zero otherwise. Zeroing torque rather than disabling the constraints leaves the wheels free-spinning, which is what lets a submarine coast rather than dragging its brakes. Before switching, the target orientation is seeded from the vehicle's current world orientation so a submarine does not snap to an arbitrary heading the instant it enters the water.

searchDocs.title: updateSubPhysics​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.updateSubPhysics() → () Recomputes the submarine rig from the vehicle's current mass. subForce is exactly mass * gravity — the force the anti-gravity VectorForce must apply to hold the vehicle neutrally buoyant, so vertical control becomes a signed offset around zero rather than a fight against gravity. The station-keeping AlignPosition gets a quarter of that, deliberately weak so it holds position without fighting the movement force. While in submarine mode it also re-anchors the hold position to where the vehicle actually is, so the rig never tries to drag it back to a stale point.

searchDocs.title: updateTorque​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.updateTorque() → () Recomputes wheel torque from the vehicle's mass and applies it to the seat and all four motors. Re-runs whenever the platform's AssemblyMass changes — that is, whenever a passenger boards or leaves — so a loaded vehicle does not become sluggish. Torque is MAX_SPEED * mass * 1.3: sizing torque against mass keeps acceleration roughly constant regardless of load, and the 1.3 is headroom for slopes. Each occupant additionally adds a flat 100 to the mass estimate, because character assemblies are not part of the vehicle's AssemblyMass. Always calls VehicleController.updateSubPhysics first — which is also what re-reads the true assembly mass — then returns early unless the state is driving, since torque means nothing in submarine mode.

searchDocs.title: startControl​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.startControl() → () Takes control of the vehicle: binds the physics loop to Heartbeat, refreshes torque, raises ClientState.inVehicle, reconfigures the camera for driving (classic mode, wide zoom range, subject back on the humanoid) and plays the seatbelt SFX. It also binds a sink action over the gameplay inputs that would otherwise fire while driving — left click, E, R, G and the equivalent gamepad buttons. Right mouse button is deliberately not sunk, because that is camera orbit. Called from the VEHICLE_START_CONTROL subscription, not directly.

searchDocs.title: stopControl​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.stopControl() → () Releases control: zeroes every throttle and steering input, holds all four wheels at zero angular velocity with full torque (so the vehicle brakes and stays put rather than rolling away driverless), clearsClientState.inVehicle, and unbinds the input sink. Finally it reports the distance travelled to the server viaVEHICLE_LOG_DISTANCE and resets the counter — dismounting is the only time the odometer is flushed, so a client that never dismounts never banks the stat. Called both from the VEHICLE_START_CONTROL subscription and from the car's Destroying handler.

searchDocs.title: updateCar​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.updateCar( deltaTime: number-- Frame delta from Heartbeat ) → () One frame of car physics. Called by VehicleController.update while the state is driving. Steering. The seat's SteerFloat is scaled to MAX_STEER_ANGLE and approached exponentially rather than snapped. The approach rate itself scales with speed (8 at idle up to 38 at full throttle), so parking manoeuvres feel weighty while highway corrections feel sharp. Both front spring attachments are then oriented to the resulting angle — this is the Ackermann knuckle rotation; the wheels themselves are driven separately below. Throttle. ThrottleFloat is approached at THROTTLE_ACCELERATION and clamped to ±1, then multiplied by MAX_SPEED and the car's SpeedMultiplier attribute (set by the server from the vehicle's upgrades). Below 10% input the throttle bleeds toward zero, which is the engine-braking feel — releasing the key coasts to a stop instead of freewheeling. Differential. Rather than computing true Ackermann per-wheel speeds, the inner wheels are simply slowed proportionally to steering lock (up to 60% at full lock). The resulting speed difference across the axle produces a yaw moment that helps the car rotate, which is cheaper and more forgiving than geometric Ackermann on Roblox's constraint solver. Right-side wheels take the negated speed because they face the opposite way. Odometer. Per-frame displacement is accumulated, ignoring sub-0.1-stud deltas so physics jitter on a parked car does not inflate the total.

searchDocs.title: updateSubmarine​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.updateSubmarine( deltaTime: number-- Frame delta from Heartbeat ) → () One frame of submarine physics. Called by VehicleController.update while the state is submarine. Underwater the camera is the control surface. Steering input yaws the camera (lerped, not snapped), the vehicle's AlignOrientation then chases the camera's heading, and the camera's pitch — offset by THROTTLE_VERTICAL_DEGREE_OFFSET and normalized against THROTTLE_MAX_VERTICAL_DEGREE — becomes the dive/climb command. Looking down while accelerating dives; looking up climbs. Vertical speed is scaled by throttle magnitude, so pointing the camera down while stationary does nothing. Throttle and steering both ease toward their goals and bleed back to zero below 10% input, the same engine-braking feel as the car. All submarine speeds are additionally scaled by SUBMARINE_SPEED_DAMPENING so the vehicle feels heavier in water than on land. Two forces do the work: subMovementForce drives lateral and forward motion in the vehicle's own frame, and subAntiGravity carries the neutral-buoyancy baseline (mass * gravity) plus the vertical command on top. Because vertical control is an offset around neutral buoyancy, releasing the controls leaves the vehicle hovering rather than sinking.

searchDocs.title: update​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.update( deltaTime: number-- Frame delta from Heartbeat ) → () Per-frame driver bound to Heartbeat by VehicleController.startControl. Handles what is common to both modes, then dispatches to VehicleController.updateCar or VehicleController.updateSubmarine. Idle station-keeping. After CAR_IDLE_TIME with no input, a submarine engages its AlignPosition and re-anchors the hold point every 0.2s. That is what stops a released submarine from drifting with residual velocity; a car needs no equivalent because friction handles it. Empty seat. If nobody is in the driver's seat, throttle is zeroed and all four wheels are held at zero velocity with full torque, and the frame ends there — an unoccupied vehicle brakes rather than coasting. This is a safety net for the window between the occupant leaving and VehicleController.stopControl running.

searchDocs.title: showPrompts​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.showPrompts( value: boolean-- true to show the prompt ) → () Enables or disables the vehicle's enter prompt. Turned off while driving so the prompt does not sit on screen in front of the seated player.

searchDocs.title: isControllingVehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.isControllingVehicle() → boolean Whether this client is currently driving. Other systems use this to suppress behaviour that would conflict with driving.

searchDocs.title: carLookAt​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.carLookAt( position: Vector3 -- World point to face ) → () Rotates the vehicle to face position over a one-second eased tween, keeping it level — the target is flattened onto the vehicle's own Y plane, so this only ever changes yaw. Implemented by tweening a scratch CFrameValue and piping its Changed into PivotTo, since models cannot be tweened directly. All three temporaries are cleaned up afterwards. Yields until the tween completes.

searchDocs.title: isLookingInDirectionOfPosition​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.isLookingInDirectionOfPosition( position: Vector3 -- World point to test against ) → boolean Whether the vehicle is roughly pointed at position. Both the vehicle's look vector and the direction to the target are flattened to the horizontal plane, so pitch is ignored; the test is dot > LOOK_ANGLE (0.95), about an 18° cone.

searchDocs.title: setCarAnchoring​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.setCarAnchoring( state: boolean-- true to anchor ) → () Anchors or un-anchors the vehicle by toggling Anchored on the driver's seat, which is the assembly's root — anchoring the seat freezes the whole vehicle. Used to pin a vehicle in place for scripted moments.

searchDocs.title: spawn​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleController.spawn() → () Toggle handler for the spawn button: despawns the current vehicle if one is live, otherwise finds a legal spot and asks the server to spawn one. Debounced, so a double-tap cannot fire two requests. Placement is resolved entirely client-side before the request goes out, in two steps: Ground find. A point SPAWN_DISTANCE studs in front of the player is raycast straight down (from 10 studs up, 100 studs deep) to find the floor. No floor means no spawn — this is what stops a vehicle appearing over a ledge or above water. Clearance check. A temporary invisible part the size of the car model's bounding box is placed at the resolved spot and GetPartsInPart is run against it. Any hit aborts. Both queries filter against the same list of Spawner- and Water-tagged instances, so spawn pads and water do not count as obstructions. The car is dropped 2 studs above the floor hit and raised by half its own height, keeping its original yaw. The server re-validates; this check exists to give immediate feedback and to avoid spamming rejected requests.

searchDocs.title: init​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.init() → () Bootstrap hook. Registers the Handlers folder with red, which is what makes VEHICLE_SPAWN, VEHICLE_DESPAWN and VEHICLE_LOG_DISTANCE reachable from clients. No-ops entirely when the Vehicle feature flag is off — with it disabled there is no client-reachable surface at all.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.start() → () Bootstrap hook. Despawns a leaving player's vehicle and clears their debounce, so a car cannot outlive its owner. No-ops entirely when the Vehicle feature flag is off.

searchDocs.title: spawnVehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.spawnVehicle( player: Player -- Owner of the new vehicle ) → Model? -- The spawned car, or nil Spawns a vehicle for player and returns its model, or nil if it could not be placed. Refused outright in the lobby (PlaceUtility.isLobby) and while the player's one-second debounce is active. Any existing vehicle is despawned first, which is what enforces one vehicle per player — this is a replace, not an add. Placement itself is decided by Vehicle.new, which re-runs the same ground and clearance checks the client did before asking; a nil from there means no legal spot and is returned as-is. On success it starts the vehicle's idle despawn timer, wires the occupancy bridge, records an analytics event, and fires VehicleSpawned.

searchDocs.title: despawnVehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.despawnVehicle(player: Player ) → () Removes the player's vehicle and fires VehicleDespawned. No-ops if they have none. Prefers the Vehicle wrapper's Destroy so the despawn timer is cancelled and seated characters have their collision restored; falls back to destroying the bare model if the wrapper is somehow missing from the cache.

searchDocs.title: getPlayerVehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.getPlayerVehicle(player: Player ) → Model?  Returns the player's current vehicle model, or nil.

searchDocs.title: getAttachmentConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.getAttachmentConfig(attachmentName: string) → VehicleAttachmentData.AttachmentConfig? Looks up an attachment's config (its slot type and model) inVehicleAttachmentData. Returns nil for an unknown name.

searchDocs.title: equipAttachment​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.equipAttachment( player: Player , attachmentName: string-- Key into VehicleAttachmentData ) → boolean-- Whether the attachment is now equipped Equips an attachment onto the player's vehicle. Slots hold one attachment each: whatever currently occupiesconfig.attachmentType is removed first, so equipping is idempotent and swapping needs no explicit unequip. Returns false for an unknown attachment name, a player with no vehicle, or a failed attach (bad slot, model without a PrimaryPart).

searchDocs.title: unequipAttachment​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.unequipAttachment( player: Player , attachmentType: string-- Slot to clear ) → boolean-- Whether something was removed Removes whatever is in the given slot on the player's vehicle. Note this takes a slot type, not an attachment name — the same key VehicleService.equipAttachment derives from the config.

searchDocs.title: getAttachmentAtSlot​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.getAttachmentAtSlot( player: Player , attachmentSlot: string ) → Model?  Returns the attachment model in the given slot on the player's vehicle, ornil.

searchDocs.title: getAllAttachments​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.getAllAttachments(player: Player ) → {[string]: Model }? Returns the player's vehicle's whole slot-to-model attachment map, or nil if they have no vehicle. The returned table is the vehicle's live map, not a copy.

searchDocs.title: setSpeedMultiplier​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.setSpeedMultiplier( player: Player , multiplier: number-- 0..1 ) → () Scales the player's vehicle's top speed. The value is written to the car'sSpeedMultiplier attribute and read by the driving client each frame, so it takes effect immediately without a remote. Clamped to 0..1 by Vehicle:SetSpeedMultiplier — this can only ever slow a vehicle down, and 0 is a full stop.

searchDocs.title: brake​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.brake(player: Player ) → () Cuts the player's vehicle to zero speed by setting its multiplier to 0. The multiplier stays at 0 until something raises it — taking the driver's seat resets it to 1.

searchDocs.title: ejectDriver​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.ejectDriver( player: Player -- Owner of the vehicle, not necessarily the driver ) → () Forcibly removes the driver from the player's vehicle, placing them on the ground beside it.

searchDocs.title: ejectPassenger​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.ejectPassenger( player: Player -- Owner of the vehicle ) → () Forcibly removes the passenger from the player's vehicle.

searchDocs.title: ejectAll​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.ejectAll( player: Player -- Owner of the vehicle ) → () Empties the player's vehicle — driver and passenger both.

searchDocs.title: ejectPlayer​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.ejectPlayer( vehicleOwner: Player ,-- Whose vehicle to act on targetPlayer: Player -- The occupant to remove ) → () Ejects one specific occupant from a vehicle, whichever seat they are in. No-ops if the target is not aboard.

searchDocs.title: logDistanceDriven​
searchDocs.content: </> VehicleService.logDistanceDriven( player: Player , distance: number-- Studs travelled this session ) → () Credits distance driven to the player's profile and records it in analytics. Called from the VEHICLE_LOG_DISTANCE handler when a driver dismounts, so the value originates on the client. It is capped at what a car could cover since the last credit (or the player's first spawn); a player who never spawned a vehicle this session is credited nothing. ProfileService is required lazily inside the function to avoid a require-time cycle between the two services.

searchDocs.title: CarState​
searchDocs.content: </> type CarState = "driving" | "submarine" Which locomotion mode a car is in. Submarine mode is entered underwater and changes how the body is driven.

searchDocs.title: Vehicle​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Vehicle { car: Model -- Root model of the spawned vehicle driverSeat: VehicleSeat -- Seat that grants control passengerSeat: VehicleSeat -- Second seat, no control body: BasePart -- Main physics body the constraints drive locked: boolean-- Non-owners are blocked from sitting maid: Maid.Maid-- Owns every connection and instance for this vehicle owner: Player -- Player the vehicle was spawned for occupiedDriver: Player? -- Whoever is in the driver seat right now occupiedPassenger: Player? -- Whoever is in the passenger seat right now occupiedSignal: Signal.Signal<Player, string>-- Fires (player, seatName) on occupancy changes attachments: {[string]: Model }-- Cosmetic or functional add-ons, keyed by slot lastSatInCar: number-- Timestamp used by the idle-despawn timer timerThread: thread?-- The pending despawn task, if one is scheduled } One spawned vehicle and everything attached to it. lastSatInCar and timerThread implement idle cleanup: leaving the vehicle schedules a despawn, and getting back in cancels it. Destroying maid releases the model, its connections and that timer together.

searchDocs.title: SpawnPayload​
searchDocs.content: </> type SpawnPayload = {} Request to spawn the player's vehicle. Currently empty — which vehicle and where are both resolved server-side from the player's profile and base. Fields are reserved for future use.

searchDocs.title: DespawnPayload​
searchDocs.content: </> type DespawnPayload = {} Request to despawn the player's vehicle. Empty for the same reason asSpawnPayload — a player has at most one vehicle, so there is nothing to name.

searchDocs.title: startVoting​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.startVoting(payload: { pool: {MinigameTypes.VotePoolItem}?, voters: {Player }? }) → () Opens a vote over payload.pool for payload.voters, zeroing the tallies and telling those clients to show the vote UI. No-ops if either the pool or the voter list is missing. If a vote is somehow already running it is stopped first, so state never bleeds between rounds.

searchDocs.title: startPlayerVote​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.startPlayerVote(player: Player ) → boolean-- Whether they were added Adds a player to an already-running vote and sends them the current pool. Used for players who load in mid-vote. Returns false if they are already eligible or have already voted. Note this grows voters, which raises the bar for the "everyone has voted" early exit — deliberately, so a late joiner is not disenfranchised by the vote closing the instant they appear.

searchDocs.title: results​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.results() → {[string]: number} Returns the current tallies as { [gameModeName]: voteCount }. Broadcast to clients after every ballot so the vote cards update live.

searchDocs.title: stop​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.stop() → () Closes the vote: clears the voting flag, fires VoteEnded, and tells all clients to dismiss the vote UI. Guarded by the voting flag, so the redundant calls from both the timeout path and the all-voted path cannot double-fire VoteEnded. Does not clear the pool or tallies — VoteService.getWinner does that, so the results survive long enough to be read.

searchDocs.title: isPlayerVoting​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.isPlayerVoting(player: Player ) → boolean Whether a player is eligible to vote in the current round. Eligibility, not participation — see VoteService.hasVoted.

searchDocs.title: hasVoted​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.hasVoted(player: Player ) → boolean Whether a player has already cast a ballot this round.

searchDocs.title: cast​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.cast( player: Player ,-- The voter payload: string-- Name of the game mode being voted for ) → () Records a player's vote for a game mode. :::info Gated by FeatureFlags.VoteChange When that flag is off — the default — a player who has already voted is silently ignored, making the first ballot final. With it on, the previous vote is decremented and the new one incremented, so players may switch freely until the vote closes. ::: Ignores votes when no vote is running, the payload is empty, or the player is not eligible. Players holding the double_votes gamepass move the tally by 2 rather than 1, applied to both the decrement and the increment so a changed weighted vote stays balanced. Broadcasts the updated tallies to everyone, then closes the vote if every eligible player has now voted.

searchDocs.title: getWinner​
searchDocs.content: </> VoteService.getWinner() → MinigameTypes.VotePoolItem Returns the winning candidate and resets the vote state. Seeded with a random pool entry so a round where nobody voted still produces a playable game, then replaced by whichever mode has the strictly highest tally. Strict comparison means a tie is resolved in favour of whichever mode iteration reached first — effectively arbitrary, which is acceptable for a tie. Clears voters, pool and votes on the way out, so this may only be called once per vote.

searchDocs.title: WaitForPrimaryPart​
searchDocs.content: </> WaitForPrimaryPart.WaitForPrimaryPart( model: Model ,-- Model to wait on timeout: number?-- Seconds to wait before giving up (defaults to 5) ) → BasePart? -- The primary part, or nil if the timeout elapsed Returns the model's PrimaryPart, waiting for it to appear if it is not set yet. Returns immediately when the PrimaryPart already exists, and returns nil if the timeout passes without one being assigned — always check the result. local root = WaitForPrimaryPart(character, 10) if root then root.CFrame = spawnCFrame end

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Zone.new( part: BasePart ,-- Volume defining the zone config: ZoneConfig-- Zone options; show keeps the part visible for debugging ) → ZoneType Creates a zone from a part, firing its signals as players enter and leave. Errors if part is missing, or if config is neither a table nor nil.

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie.new( model: Model ,-- the rig to drive config: ZombieTypes.ZombieConfig-- health, animations and behaviour tuning ) → Zombie Wraps a rig model in a Zombie, registering any per-state animations declared on the config with the underlying Freshynoid. The zombie starts in the Idle state with full health, and mirrors its health onto the model as the Health and MaxHealth attributes so other systems can read it without holding a reference to this object.

searchDocs.title: SetState​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:SetState( stateName: ZombieTypes.ZombieStateName-- state to enter ) → () Transitions the zombie into a new AI state. Stops the outgoing state module, records it as previousState, then starts the incoming one. No-ops when already in the requested state, and refuses every transition except Death once the zombie is dead. When the config declares a behaviorOverride, that module is started instead of the built-in state module for the new state.

searchDocs.title: Step​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:Step( dt: number-- seconds elapsed since the previous step ) → () Advances the active state by one tick. Called by the owning zombie manager every frame (or less often for distant zombies, per lodTier). Dead zombies are skipped entirely. A configured behaviorOverride that implements Step replaces the built-in state's step for this tick.

searchDocs.title: TakeDamage​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:TakeDamage( amount: number-- damage to apply ) → () Subtracts damage from the zombie's health, clamped at zero, and republishes the new value to the model's Health attribute. Calls Zombie:Die once health reaches zero. No-ops on an already dead zombie.

searchDocs.title: Die​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:Die() → () Marks the zombie dead, transitions it into the Death state (which plays the death animation and ragdolls the rig) and fires Died. Idempotent. The zombie object is not destroyed here — the owner is expected to callZombie:Destroy after the death sequence has played out.

searchDocs.title: GetTarget​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:GetTarget() → ZombieTypes.ZombieTarget? Returns the zombie's current target, or nil when it has none. The target is selected by the Seek/Chase states according to targetMode.

searchDocs.title: GetPosition​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:GetPosition() → Vector3  Returns the world position of the underlying rig.

searchDocs.title: GetModel​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:GetModel() → Model  Returns the rig model this zombie drives.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Zombie:Destroy() → () Tears the zombie down: stops the active state (skipped when already inDeath, which owns its own cleanup), destroys the Died signal and destroys the underlying NPC and its rig.
